9.grammar: The word ends in a fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra) marking its feminine noun-form, which does not change for case. The attached -hum means 'their', referring to a group of males (or a mixed group), and marks possession: 'their call/plea'.
9.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, to invoke, to summon

10.meaning: That — an explanatory particle introducing the content of a preceding statement or command, roughly 'namely that …' or 'to the effect that …'. It unpacks what was said or commanded.
10.grammar: An explanatory particle 'an' meaning 'that / namely,' used to spell out the substance of a foregoing verb of saying or commanding (so the words that follow explain it). Its base form ends in a vowel-less 'n'; the -i shown here is a helping vowel added only to ease pronunciation before a following consonant, not a case ending.

11.meaning: The praise — all commendation, thanks, and laudation. With the article it conveys praise as a whole, in its entirety, belonging by right to the one praised.
11.grammar: A verbal noun with the definite article 'al-'. The '-u' ending is nominative, marking it as the subject/topic of a sentence; with the article it carries the sense of 'all praise' as an entire, comprehensive category.
11.root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d) — to praise/commend

12.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
12.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

13.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
13.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
13.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

14.meaning: 'The worlds / all created beings' — the entirety of created realms and their inhabitants (humans, jinn, and everything else); a plural conveying 'all that exists'.
14.grammar: A definite masculine sound plural. The '-īna' ending marks the plural in the object/genitive state (used as a non-subject, after a preposition, or after certain particles), as opposed to the subject form '-ūna'.
14.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; (ʿālam) a world, a domain of knowing/created order

1.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
1.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

2.meaning: he hastens, hurries, or brings something on quickly — to bring a thing forward before its due time.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in an intensive/causative stem ('to make haste with, hurry something along'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he'. The final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a real, ongoing or habitual action (as opposed to a command or a 'so that' clause).

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
4.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.

5.meaning: the evil, harm, or bad thing — what is injurious, wicked, or undesirable.
5.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -a ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or follows certain particles. The 'sh' absorbs the 'l' of 'al-' in pronunciation.
5.root: ش-ر-ر (sh-r-r) — evil, badness, harm

6.meaning: their seeking to hasten something — the act of asking for or demanding that a thing be brought on quickly.

parts.en: seeking to hasten / asking for speed

6.grammar: A verbal noun from the 'seeking/requesting' stem, meaning the act of trying to make something come faster, with an attached possessive. The -a ending is accusative (object case). The -hum means 'their' (masculine plural).

7.meaning: with, or in regard to, the good — that which is beneficial, wholesome, and desirable.
7.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with / in / for') attached to a noun carrying the definite article al- ('the'). The preposition puts the noun in the genitive, which is the -i ending. The noun denotes goodness or benefit, and can also mean 'better / best'.
7.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, benefit

8.meaning: 'Surely it would have been decided / settled / carried out' — a past-tense passive: the matter would have been judged and brought to completion. The opening particle adds emphasis ('surely / certainly').
8.grammar: A past-tense passive verb ('was decided', not 'he decided') preceded by the emphatic particle 'la-' ('surely'). The vowel pattern (u–i) signals the passive voice — the action is done to the subject by an unnamed doer. It is the singular masculine 'it/he' form.

9.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
9.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
9.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

10.meaning: 'Their term / appointed time' — the fixed span or deadline set for them, the determined point at which something is due to end or occur. Belonging to a plural 'them'.
10.grammar: A noun carrying the possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their'). The '-u' before the pronoun marks the nominative case, the base form a noun takes as the subject of a sentence or when standing in that primary state.
10.root: ا-ج-ل (ʾ-j-l) — appointed term, fixed span of time

11.meaning: so We leave, let alone, or forsake — to let something remain as it is without intervening.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb meaning 'to leave / let be'. The na- prefix means 'we'. The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a genuine ongoing or habitual action. The opening fa- is a connector meaning 'so / then', often showing result or sequence.
11.root: و-ذ-ر (w-dh-r) — to leave, abandon, let alone

12.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
12.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

13.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
13.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

14.meaning: They hold out hope for something, expecting and longing for a good outcome (often divine reward or mercy). The verb can carry both hoping for good and, in some contexts, fearing/anticipating.
14.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The -ūna ending is the indicative form, signalling a real, ongoing or habitual action ('they hope / they keep hoping').

15.meaning: A meeting or encounter — the coming face to face with someone. With the attached pronoun it means 'meeting Us / the encounter with Us', often used of standing before Allah.
15.grammar: A verbal noun ('a meeting') with the attached pronoun '-nā' ('us/our'). The '-a' before the pronoun marks the accusative case, typically identifying the object of a verb; the pronoun then names the one met ('the meeting OF Us'). As a verbal noun it carries the sense of the act of meeting.
15.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — meeting, encountering

16.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
16.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

17.meaning: Their overstepping of bounds — rebellious excess, tyranny, and inordinate transgression that exceeds all proper limits, especially against the truth. The attached pronoun marks it as belonging to them.
17.grammar: A verbal noun (naming the act/state of overstepping bounds) with the attached possessive -him ('their,' for a group of males). The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, marking possession ('… of theirs') or governance by a preceding preposition.
17.root: ط-غ-ي (ṭ-gh-y) — to overflow, exceed all bounds, be tyrannical

18.meaning: They wander about blindly and perplexed — moving to and fro in confusion and bewilderment, unable to see their way. Conveys aimless, dazed straying.
18.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males), and the full -ūna (not shortened) marks the indicative mood, a plain statement of ongoing action: 'they wander blindly.'
18.root: ع-م-ه (ʿ-m-h) — to wander in confusion, be dazed and blindly perplexed

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: Touched, afflicted, or befell — for something (such as harm or hardship) to have made contact with someone.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he/it touched'). The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for a single masculine subject; the doubled middle consonant (shadda) is part of this root's basic form.
2.root: م-س-س (m-s-s) — to touch, make contact, afflict

3.meaning: the human being, mankind — the human creature in general, marked by sociability and forgetfulness.
3.grammar: A noun for the human being, with the definite article al- ('the'). The -a ending is accusative, typically marking the direct object of a verb or following certain particles. Used generically, it denotes humankind as a type.
3.root: أ-ن-س ('-n-s) — to be sociable, familiar; humanness

4.meaning: the harm, distress, injury, or adversity — affliction that touches a person, such as illness, hardship, or loss.
4.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence (the doer or the thing 'that …'). The 'ḍ' absorbs the 'l' of 'al-' in pronunciation.

5.meaning: he called upon Us, invoked Us, or appealed to Us — a calling out in prayer or for help.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb meaning 'to call, invoke, or supplicate'. With no added subject-ending it carries the default third-person masculine singular, 'he … '. The attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us', the one being called upon.
5.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, pray

6.meaning: for, or on, his side — referring to lying down on one's side, as a posture of rest or of being bedridden.
6.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / on') attached to a noun meaning 'side', with a possessive pronoun. The preposition puts the noun in the genitive — the -i vowel seen before the pronoun. The attached -hi means 'his'.
6.root: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b) — side, flank; to be beside

7.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
7.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

8.meaning: sitting, seated, or in a sitting posture — one who is sitting down.
8.grammar: An active participle naming the one performing the act — 'a sitting / seated person'. The -an ending is accusative and indefinite ('a sitter'), the case often used for a describing state ('while sitting') or as an object. It carries no 'the', so it is indefinite.

9.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
9.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

10.meaning: Standing, upright, and maintaining — one who stands firm and upholds or carries out something; by extension, sustaining and establishing a matter with steady constancy.
10.grammar: A masculine active participle ('one who stands / upholds'), indefinite. The final -an (nunation) marks it accusative and indefinite — the case typically used for an object or, very commonly for a participle like this, to describe the state or manner in which someone is ('… while standing / upholding').

11.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
11.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

12.meaning: 'We removed / we lifted off / we uncovered.' The verb means to take away a covering, to lift off a burden or affliction, to disclose or lay bare. It often describes the relieving of a hardship or the unveiling of something hidden.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb (Form I) in the 'we' person. The bare stem kashaf- carries the completed-action (past) sense, and the attached -nā ending means 'we' as the doers ('we removed / we lifted'). The -nā suffix on a past verb always marks a first-person plural subject that has already performed the act.
12.root: ك-ش-ف (k-sh-f) — to uncover, remove a covering, disclose

13.meaning: A combination meaning 'from him / from it / about him.' The preposition denotes moving away from, departing from, or concerning a thing, and the pronoun refers to a single masculine entity.
13.grammar: A preposition with a fused object pronoun. ʿan governs the genitive and conveys separation or 'concerning.' The attached -hu marks a third-person masculine singular object ('him/it').

14.meaning: his harm, distress, or affliction — the adversity that befalls a particular person.
14.grammar: A noun for harm or distress with an attached possessive. The -a ending is accusative, typically marking the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The -hu means 'his'.

15.meaning: he passed / he passed by — a third-person past verb meaning to go past, to pass through or by a place or thing.
15.grammar: A past tense verb with a third-person singular masculine doer ('he'). The doubled final consonant reflects the root's repeated letter. The final -a marks the third-person singular masculine subject. It states a completed action: 'he passed'.
15.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — to pass, to pass by

16.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'as if / as though.' It introduces a comparison or likeness, treating a situation as resembling another — presenting something as if it were a certain way, whether or not it truly is.
16.grammar: A particle of comparison formed from 'ka-' ('like / as') joined to a particle meaning 'that.' Together they function as a single linking word, 'as if,' used to liken one circumstance to another. It is a particle, so it has no case ending of its own.

17.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
17.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

18.meaning: he calls upon Us, invokes Us, or appeals to Us — an ongoing or repeated calling out in prayer or for help.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb meaning 'to call or invoke'. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he'. The attached object pronoun -nā ('us') is the one being called. The final weak letter of the root is dropped, leaving the bare 'yadʿu' before the pronoun.
18.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, pray

19.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
19.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

20.meaning: harm, distress, injury, or affliction — adversity such as illness, hardship, or loss (in an indefinite, unspecified sense).
20.grammar: A noun denoting harm or distress, with no 'the' so it is indefinite ('some harm / a distress'). The -in ending is genitive and indefinite, the form typically used after a preposition or in an 'of …' link to a preceding noun.

21.meaning: it touched him, befell him, or afflicted him — said of harm or experience reaching and affecting a person.
21.grammar: A past-tense verb meaning 'to touch, reach, or befall'. The third-person masculine singular subject ('he / it') is marked by a zero (null) suffix — there is no overt subject ending. The visible -a (fatḥa) on the final radical is the stem's own vowel pattern, not a person marker. The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him', the one touched or afflicted.
21.root: م-س-س (m-s-s) — to touch, come into contact, befall

22.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
22.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
22.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

23.meaning: It was made beautiful / adorned / made alluring; the act of decorating something or making it appear attractive and appealing.
23.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice on an intensive (form II) pattern, so the action is done to the subject and stresses thorough adorning ("was made beautiful/alluring"). The -u-…-i- vowel pattern marks the passive, and the final -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject ("it/he").

24.meaning: for, or to, the extravagant ones — those who exceed all proper bounds, who are wasteful and transgress limits.

parts.en: one who exceeds bounds / is wasteful

24.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to') joined to the definite article al- and an active participle, 'the one who goes to excess'. The sound masculine plural ending -īna here is the form used after a preposition (genitive), meaning 'the extravagant ones'.
24.root: س-ر-ف (s-r-f) — to exceed bounds, be wasteful, go to excess

25.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
25.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

26.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
26.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
26.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

27.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
27.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
27.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: 'We destroyed / We caused to perish' — to bring about ruin, annihilation, or downfall. Combines the verb 'to destroy / cause to perish' with the subject 'we'.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The attached '-nā' ending is the subject 'we' — it marks the doers of the action as a group including the speaker, with the action completed and in the past.
2.root: ه-ل-ك (h-l-k) — to perish, be destroyed; (causative) to destroy

3.meaning: the generations, or the long ages of people — successive communities of humankind that lived and passed away.
3.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'), denoting generations or epochs of people. The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
3.root: ق-ر-ن (q-r-n) — to join, conjoin; a generation/age (a span of joined lives)

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: 'before you,' 'prior to you' — an expression of precedence in time or place, here relating that precedence to 'you (plural).' The core word denotes the 'before' side, what comes earlier or in front.
5.grammar: An adverb of time/place ('before') joined to the pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). The '-i' ending is genitive: such words of place/time regularly take this case, especially after a preposition, and the attached pronoun completes the sense as 'before you.'
5.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — precedence, being before/in front

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the point that' something occurred — pointing to the moment a past event took place and often implying that one thing happened upon the completion of another. In other uses it can carry the sense of 'not yet'.
6.grammar: A particle (a small connecting word), not a noun or verb, so it has no case or tense ending. It introduces a clause and links it in time to another event — most often 'when / as soon as' a past action happened.

7.meaning: 'They wronged / did injustice / acted unjustly'. The core idea is putting something out of its rightful place — oppression, transgression, or wronging oneself or others.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb with the plural subject ending -ū ('they', masculine/mixed group), referring to a completed action done by many. The -ū suffix is written with a silent 'alif' after it. It states that a group performed the act of wronging.
7.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress; to put a thing out of its proper place

8.meaning: and there came to them — said of messengers, signs, or events arriving and reaching a group.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb meaning 'to come, arrive'. The -at ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she / it' came), which in Arabic also agrees with a feminine or plural-of-things subject. The attached -hum is the object 'them' (the ones reached); wa- is 'and'.

9.meaning: Their messengers — the envoys or apostles sent by Allah, here belonging to 'them'; 'rusul' is the plural of 'rasūl', one who is dispatched bearing a message.
9.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -hum ending means 'their' (for a group of males). The -u vowel before it is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a sentence.
9.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a messenger, an envoy

10.meaning: 'With the clear proofs / evident signs' — bayyināt are plain, self-evident demonstrations that make the truth manifest, leaving no doubt.
10.grammar: Built from 'bi-' ('with/by means of') + 'al-' ('the') + a feminine plural noun meaning 'clear proofs.' The -i ending is the genitive case, required after the preposition 'bi-'; the feminine sound plural '-āt' takes -i (not -a) in this case. The whole phrase means 'with the clear proofs.'

11.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
11.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

12.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
12.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

13.meaning: A verb phrase meaning 'so that they would believe' or 'in order for them to believe'. The underlying act is having faith — accepting and trusting in a truth, especially faith in Allah and His message.
13.grammar: li- is the particle 'so that / in order that', which puts the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood (expressing purpose or intended result). The verb is the Form IV present yu'minu, 'to believe / have faith'. The plural ending normally -ūna loses its final -na to become -ū because of the subjunctive, and the doer is 'they' (a group of males).

14.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
14.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
14.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

15.meaning: 'We reward / We requite' — to repay or recompense someone for their deeds, whether with good or with due consequence.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'na-' prefix means 'we'. The stem ends in a long '-ī' (a weak final root letter); in the plain indicative this final '-ī' is what is heard, giving 'we reward'.
15.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to repay, to recompense, to requite

16.meaning: the people / the folk — a body of people, a community or group regarded collectively (here in the accusative form).
16.grammar: The l- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The final -a ending is accusative. Since the verb it follows is passive (and so takes no direct object), this accusative is adverbial — marking the circumstance or setting of the action ('before / in front of the people') rather than a thing being acted upon.
16.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to arise; a people standing together

17.meaning: Those who commit grave sins and crimes; wrongdoers who deliberately break Allah's law and cut themselves off in guilt. The word denotes hardened, culpable offenders, not those who err by accident.
17.grammar: An active participle (one who does the action) of Form IV, made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) case, so it names a group as the object of a verb or the complement of a preposition, rather than the subject.
17.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to commit a crime or grave sin

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

2.meaning: 'We made / appointed / rendered you (plural)' — to bring about, establish, or designate a group as something. The verb 'ja‘ala' often means not just 'to make' physically but 'to appoint/turn into' a certain state or role.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The suffix -nā marks the subject as 'we' (the doers). The further suffix -kum is the object pronoun 'you', addressed to a group (masculine or mixed). So the verb means 'we made/appointed you (all)', describing a completed act.
2.root: ج-ع-ل (j-‘-l) — making, placing, appointing, rendering into a state

3.meaning: Successors, deputies, inheritors — those who come after others and take their place, holding a position handed on to them (as stewards or vice-gerents on the earth). It is the plural of 'khalīfah'.
3.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural on the pattern 'khalāʾif', plural of 'khalīfah' ('successor, deputy'). The final -a is the accusative case, here typically the direct object or the role assigned ('made you successors'). Such 'diptote' plurals take -a rather than -an even when indefinite. It denotes those who succeed and take others' place.
3.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, succeed, leave behind

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
5.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').
5.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: "after them / following them" — the noun baʿd ('after, afterward') with the attached pronoun 'them', denoting what comes later in time than a group.
7.grammar: A time-noun used like a preposition, with an attached pronoun. The -i ending is genitive, the form taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive link. The suffix -him means 'them' (its vowel is -hi- to harmonise with the preceding -i).
7.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, what follows

8.meaning: so that We may look, observe, or see — to watch and consider in order to find out how something will turn out.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb meaning 'to look or observe', governed by the prefixed li- ('so that / in order to'), which expresses purpose. That purpose-particle changes the usual ending to -a (the subjunctive), the form used in 'so that …' clauses. The na- prefix means 'we'.
8.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, see, observe, consider

9.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
9.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.
9.root: — (interrogative particle; no triliteral root)

10.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
10.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: It is being recited or read aloud — said of verses or scripture conveyed by voice, in an ongoing or repeated manner.

parts.en: recite/read aloud (passive stem, root letters t-l + long ā)

2.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) passive verb in the third person feminine singular ('it/she is recited'). The tu- prefix marks both the present tense and the passive voice ('is being …-ed'), so the doer is unnamed and the focus is on what undergoes the action. The stem -tlā keeps the second root consonant (t) and ends in a long ā written with ى, the shape a weak-final (defective) root takes when no further ending is attached.
2.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

3.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
3.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
3.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: Our signs, marks, or verses — tokens that point to a deeper truth, including the divinely revealed verses.
4.grammar: A feminine plural noun meaning 'signs / tokens / verses', with an attached possessive. The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence. The attached -nā means 'our'.

5.meaning: Clear, manifest, self-evident — the feminine plural of 'bayyin', describing things that are plainly evident and make matters distinct; an intensive adjective implying something that clarifies and is itself unmistakable.
5.grammar: A sound feminine plural adjective. The '-in' (nunation) ending marks it indefinite and in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case, so it agrees with an indefinite feminine plural noun it describes ('clear ___').
5.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct, evident; to make plain

6.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
6.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: They hold out hope for something, expecting and longing for a good outcome (often divine reward or mercy). The verb can carry both hoping for good and, in some contexts, fearing/anticipating.
9.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The -ūna ending is the indicative form, signalling a real, ongoing or habitual action ('they hope / they keep hoping').
9.root: ر-ج-و (r-j-w) — to hope, to expect

10.meaning: A meeting or encounter — the coming face to face with someone. With the attached pronoun it means 'meeting Us / the encounter with Us', often used of standing before Allah.
10.grammar: A verbal noun ('a meeting') with the attached pronoun '-nā' ('us/our'). The '-a' before the pronoun marks the accusative case, typically identifying the object of a verb; the pronoun then names the one met ('the meeting OF Us'). As a verbal noun it carries the sense of the act of meeting.

11.meaning: A command meaning 'bring!' or 'come with / produce!' — an imperative addressed to a single person, instructing them to bring forth or come bearing something.
11.grammar: A singular imperative verb addressed to one person ('you, bring/produce'), built on a root whose first letter is itself a hamza (ء). To make the command pronounceable, a hamzat al-waṣl (a connecting helping-vowel, dropped in connected speech) is prefixed at the front, while the original root hamza is dropped from the stem. The final -i is the imperative ending for this weak-final root, marking a direct command.
11.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, to bring, to arrive

12.meaning: 'With a recitation / with a Qur'an' — a thing that is recited or read aloud; the verbal noun came to name the recited revelation itself.
12.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with'). The final -in is the genitive case with nunation (tanwīn): the case is genitive because it follows the preposition, and the -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a recitation' rather than 'the recitation').

13.meaning: Other than / different from. A noun used to negate or exclude — it points to something that is not the thing mentioned, marking difference or absence.
13.grammar: A noun of exception/negation meaning 'something other than'. The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. So it sets up the sense 'other than [the following thing]'.

14.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
14.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

15.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
15.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

16.meaning: A command meaning 'change it! / alter it! / replace it!' — an instruction to one person to substitute or modify something.
16.grammar: A singular imperative verb of the intensive (form II) pattern, which carries the sense of actively altering or substituting. It is addressed to one person ('you, change'). The attached -hu is an object pronoun ('it/him'), the thing being changed. The sukūn (silent ending) on the verb stem is the normal jussive-style ending of a command.

17.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
17.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.
17.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak

18.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
18.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

19.meaning: 'It is / it comes to be' — the present-tense verb of being and becoming (from kāna). It expresses that something is the case, exists, or comes about.
19.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he/it is, becomes'. The ya- prefix means 'he/it', and the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain factual statement (as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form).
19.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

20.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
20.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

21.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
21.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

22.meaning: '(that) I change it / replace it' — the act of altering or substituting something, performed by the speaker.
22.grammar: A present-tense (form II, intensive) verb with the u- prefix marking the first-person singular ('I'). The stem vowel ends in -a (subjunctive mood), the form a verb takes after particles meaning 'that / so that / to', expressing an intended or hypothetical action rather than a plain statement. The attached -hu is the object pronoun ('it').
22.root: ب-د-ل (b-d-l) — to change, exchange, substitute

23.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
23.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

24.meaning: '(of) the direction / the side facing toward' — used in the phrase 'of my own accord', literally 'from what faces / comes from myself', i.e. on one's own initiative.
24.grammar: A noun (a verbal-noun pattern of 'meeting/facing') functioning to express direction or source. The final -i is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a following noun ('the side OF …') or follows a preposition, conveying 'from the direction of'.

25.meaning: 'Myself / my own soul'. The word nafs means a self, soul, person or inner being; with the attached 'my' it points to the speaker's own self.
25.grammar: Noun plus the attached possessor -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' suffix replaces the case-ending, so the noun's grammatical role (subject, object, or after a preposition) is read from context rather than from a final short vowel.

26.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
26.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

27.meaning: 'I follow / pursue / adhere to' — to go after something and take it as one's guide or example, following in its track. The form conveys actively following or conforming to something.

parts.en: follow / adhere to (present-tense stem of the 'follow closely' pattern)

27.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'a-' prefix meaning 'I'. The doubled 't' at the start of the stem belongs to the verb-pattern that means following closely or taking as a guide. The '-u' ending is the ordinary present-tense form for an ongoing action: 'I follow'.

28.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
28.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

29.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
29.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

30.meaning: 'It is revealed / is inspired' — the act of conveying something by inspiration or revelation, expressed passively (the thing is made known to someone by a higher source).
30.grammar: A present-tense passive verb (form IV) in the third-person masculine singular ('it is …'). The yu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks the passive voice — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The final weak vowel -ā (written on a yā') is the ending of this weak-final root in the present tense, here read as an ongoing/repeated passive ('is being revealed').
30.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to reveal, inspire, convey by suggestion

31.meaning: 'To me / toward me.' It joins the preposition ilā, meaning 'to / toward,' with an attached first-person 'me,' expressing motion or direction toward the speaker.
31.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to / toward' with the attached pronoun 'me.' The base preposition is ilā, ending in a long vowel (written with alif maqsūra, ى). When the 'me' pronoun attaches, that final long vowel turns into yāʾ and merges with the pronoun's yāʾ, giving a doubled, stressed -ayya — the whole word reading ilayya, 'to me.'

32.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
32.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

33.meaning: I fear, I am afraid of, I stand in awe/dread — expressing the speaker's own fear, whether dread of harm or reverent awe.
33.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks the doer as 'I'. The final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual state ('I fear / I am fearing').

34.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
34.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

35.meaning: 'I disobeyed', 'I rebelled against', 'I defied (an order)'. The verb means to go against a command and refuse obedience.
35.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -tu ending marks the subject as 'I' with the action completed: 'I disobeyed'. The stem comes from a root whose final letter is a weak letter, which surfaces here as 'ay' before the ending.

36.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
36.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
36.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

37.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
37.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.

38.meaning: a day — a day, the basic unit of daytime or a twenty-four-hour span; figuratively a time or occasion.
38.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -in ending marks the genitive case together with the indefinite 'a/an'. The genitive is the case used after prepositions or to link this noun to a preceding word ('… of a day').
38.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — a day, a span of time

39.meaning: An adjective meaning 'great', 'immense', 'mighty', or 'tremendous' — vast in size, importance, or gravity; used of things weighty and momentous.
39.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern (conveying a strong, established quality), carrying the genitive indefinite '-in' (tanwīn) ending. The genitive case typically appears after a preposition or when describing/qualifying a preceding genitive noun.
39.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense; (literally) bone, hence weightiness

1.meaning: An imperative command meaning 'Say!' or 'Speak!' — a direct order to one person to utter or declare something.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male. The bare, vowelless ending (the silent stop on the final 'l') marks it as a direct order: 'you, say!' It is built from the verb 'to say' with the weak middle letter dropped, leaving the short, clipped command form.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

2.meaning: If — a conditional particle introducing a hypothetical that is contrary to fact or unfulfilled ("if [such-and-such had been the case]…"), typically implying that because the condition did not hold, its result did not occur either.
2.grammar: A conditional particle. It has no ending to inflect. It sets up a supposed condition, classically one understood as unreal or unrealized, and is normally answered by a result clause (often introduced by la-, "surely [then]…").

3.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
3.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
4.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

5.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

6.meaning: 'I recited it / read it aloud' — the completed act, by the speaker, of reciting or reading something out.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The suffix -tu marks the first-person singular as the doer ('I did'), indicating a completed action. The attached -hu is the object pronoun ('it'), the thing recited. The root's final weak letter appears as -aw before the suffix.
6.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

7.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
7.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.
7.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

8.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

9.meaning: 'He made you (plural) know it / acquainted you with it' — to cause a group to become aware of or perceive something.
9.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) causative verb (form IV), third-person masculine singular ('he caused to know'). The final weak vowel -ā belongs to the weak-final root. The attached -kum is the object pronoun for a group ('you all'), those who are made aware.
9.root: د-ر-ي (d-r-y) — to know, be aware, perceive

10.meaning: 'With it / by it / about it' — a preposition joined to a pronoun, pointing back to a previously mentioned thing.
10.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/by') fused with the third-person masculine singular pronoun. The pronoun takes the -hi form (rather than -hu) because it follows a word ending in the -i sound; it refers back to a previously mentioned masculine thing.

11.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
11.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

12.meaning: I stayed / I remained / I tarried — a past verb meaning to remain or abide for a period, with the speaker as the one who stayed.
12.grammar: A past tense verb meaning to stay or linger. The suffix -tu marks the doer as first-person singular ('I'), stating 'I remained' — a completed staying in the past.

13.meaning: Among you / in you: locates something within a group of people addressed in the plural.
13.grammar: A preposition 'in/among' with an attached pronoun -kum meaning 'you' for a group of males (or mixed group). Words after the preposition fī stand in the genitive, which is why the pronoun takes this object form. The whole expresses presence or location within the addressed group.

14.meaning: 'A lifetime / lifespan / age' — the span of one's life or the length of time one has lived.
14.grammar: A noun in the accusative case with nunation (tanwīn). The -an ending typically marks the object of a verb or a span/extent ('for a lifetime'), and the -n sound shows it is indefinite ('a lifetime').
14.root: ع-م-ر (ʿ-m-r) — to live long, to inhabit, life-span

15.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
15.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

16.meaning: Before; the period or point in time (or place) prior to something. With the attached pronoun it means 'before it / before him', pointing to what came earlier.
16.grammar: An adverb/noun of time meaning 'before', functioning here as something governed in the genitive (the -i ending), as it regularly follows a preposition such as 'from'. The attached -hi means 'it / him' ('before it'); the vowel of the pronoun is -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows the -i ending.
16.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede; front, priorness

17.meaning: 'Then will you not…?' — a rhetorical opener combining 'then/so,' a question, and a negation, used to prompt reflection ('do you then not…?').
17.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb: the question marker 'a-' ('?'), the connector 'fa-' ('then/so'), and the negator 'lā' ('not'). Together they form a rhetorical question expecting agreement — 'will you then not…?' It has no case or tense ending of its own.

18.meaning: 'You understand / use reason' — to comprehend, think, and grasp matters with the intellect; to apply sound reasoning.
18.grammar: The prefix 'ta-' marks a 2nd-person present-tense verb, and the '-ūna' ending makes the subject a masculine-inclusive plural 'you all.' The '-ūna' is the indicative marker, signalling a plain factual or ongoing statement.
18.root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l) — to reason, understand, be intelligent

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
1.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

2.meaning: An elative adjective meaning 'more / most wrongdoing, unjust, or oppressive' — comparing degrees of ẓulm (placing things out of their rightful place, transgression).
2.grammar: An elative (comparative/superlative) noun on the pattern afʿal, meaning 'more/most unjust'. It ends in -u (nominative), the case typical of a subject or predicate.
2.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, putting something where it does not belong

3.meaning: A combination meaning 'than whoever / than one who' or 'from whoever' — the preposition min ('from/than') merged with man ('who/whoever'). It links a comparison or origin to an unspecified person.
3.grammar: The preposition min ('from', and 'than' in comparisons) fused with the relative/indefinite pronoun man ('who(ever)'). The nūn of min assimilates into the mīm of man, so min + man becomes mimman. The whole final nūn belongs to man, not to min; the kasrah on it (-i) is a liaison (waṣl) vowel added to keep two unvowelled consonants (sukūns) from meeting before the next word. Read together: mimmani, 'than/from the one who'.

4.meaning: 'He fabricated, invented, forged (a lie); he concocted falsely' — made something up and falsely attributed it, especially a lie. A verb of deliberate fabrication.

parts.en: connecting (helping) vowel for the verb pattern
past-tense 3rd person masculine singular ending '-ā' (from a weak final root letter)

4.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he fabricated'). It is a Form VIII (ifta'ala) verb. The final '-ā' (written as alif maqṣūra) is how the past-tense '-a' ending appears when the root ends in a weak letter (w/y). The initial 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the consonant cluster of this pattern be pronounced.
4.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to fabricate, forge, invent (a falsehood)

5.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
5.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
5.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'a lie / falsehood' — a deliberately false statement, an untruth fabricated against the truth.
7.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a lie') with the accusative -an ending (tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks the object of a verb (e.g. fabricating a lie); the -an tanwīn shows it is indefinite.
7.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, to declare false

8.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
8.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'he denied / cried lies against / rejected as false' — to treat something or someone as a lie, refusing to accept it as true and openly rejecting it.
9.grammar: Past-tense verb (form II, intensive), third-person masculine singular ('he denied / rejected as false'). The doubled middle letter (kadhdhaba) gives the sense of actively declaring something false. The final -a is the past-tense ending for a masculine singular doer.
9.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; (form II) to deny, to call a lie

10.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in / by His signs' — the preposition bi- ('with/in/by') joined to āyāt ('signs, verses, tokens') and 'His'. Āyāt are signs or proofs pointing to Allah, including revealed verses and observable signs.
10.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in/by/with') governing the plural noun āyāt ('signs'), which takes the genitive -i ending because it follows a preposition; the attached -hi means 'His'. The genitive is the case used after prepositions and to show possession ('signs OF His'). The pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) in harmony with the preceding -i vowel.

11.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
11.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

12.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
12.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

13.meaning: A verb meaning 'he succeeds / prospers / attains salvation' — to thrive and reach what is sought while escaping what is feared; ultimate well-being and triumph, including success in the Hereafter.
13.grammar: Present-tense verb (form IV), third-person masculine singular ('he succeeds'). The yu- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending for a plain present statement.
13.root: ف-ل-ح (f-l-ḥ) — to prosper, succeed, attain, be saved

14.meaning: The criminals, the guilty, the wrongdoers — those who deliberately commit grave sins and cut themselves off from what is right.
14.grammar: A noun (active participle, 'one who commits crime/sin') with the definite article al-, in the masculine plural. The '-ūna' ending is the sound masculine plural in the nominative — the form used when such people are the subject/doer, marking 'the ones who…' as the actors.
14.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to commit a crime or grave sin, guilt

1.meaning: 'And they worship / serve' — a group devoting themselves in worship and obedient service to something.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna pattern marks the third-person masculine plural ('they'). The retained -na ending shows the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('they do worship'), as opposed to the moods that drop this -n.

2.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
2.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

3.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
3.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
3.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

6.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
6.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

7.meaning: It harms them; it injures or damages them. The verb 'to harm' with 'them' as the ones harmed.
7.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'), with the attached object pronoun -hum ('them'). The ya- prefix marks present tense and a single (or unspecified) doer; -hum is the receiver of the action.
7.root: ض-ر-ر (ḍ-r-r) — to harm, injure, damage

8.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

9.meaning: It benefits them; it brings them profit, advantage, or good. Built on the verb meaning to be of use or to do good to someone, with an attached object 'them'.
9.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'), shown by the ya- prefix. The -u ending marks the ordinary indicative mood (a plain statement of present or future action). The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them'.
9.root: ن-ف-ع (n-f-ʿ) — to benefit, profit, be of use

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'and they say / and they keep saying' — to utter or assert in speech. The structure presents an ongoing or repeated act of speaking by a group.
10.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb joined by wa- ('and'). The ya-…-ūna frame marks the 3rd-person masculine plural ('they'); the full -ūna ending is the inseparable indicative-plural suffix, showing the verb is in its base (indicative) form and expressing an ongoing or habitual action.

11.meaning: These / those — a plural demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things. Its core sense is the near demonstrative 'these', but it is very commonly rendered 'those' in translation when the group it points to has already been described or named rather than being physically present.
11.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, used for a group of either gender. Its base value is near-deixis ('these'), built from an attention-drawing prefix 'hā-' ('lo!, here') plus the base 'ulāʾi'. In practice it is often translated 'those' when the referent is already mentioned or understood rather than literally nearby. Its form is fixed and does not change for grammatical case; it points to a group rather than naming it.

12.meaning: 'Our intercessors' — those who plead or mediate on someone's behalf, here belonging to 'us'.
12.grammar: A plural noun ('intercessors') with the possessive pronoun -nā ('our') attached. The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described/named.

13.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
13.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

14.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
14.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

15.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
15.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.
15.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak

16.meaning: 'Do you (plural) inform / tell / notify?' — a question put to a group: are you announcing or making something known?
16.grammar: Opens with the interrogative prefix a- ('do…?', turning the statement into a question). The verb is present-tense, intensive (form II), with the tu-…-ūna pattern marking the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The retained -na ending is the indicative mood, a plain present ('you inform').
16.root: ن-ب-ء (n-b-ʾ) — to inform, announce, bring news

17.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
17.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
17.root: — (proper name)

18.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
18.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

19.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
19.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

20.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
20.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
20.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

21.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
21.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

22.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
22.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.
22.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, sky

23.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
23.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

24.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
24.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

25.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
25.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

26.meaning: An exclamation of glorification meaning 'far removed and utterly above all imperfection is He.' The verbal noun 'subḥān' declares that the One referred to is exalted beyond any deficiency, partner, or fault, and the attached 'Him' directs that declaration to a single masculine being.
