6.meaning: 'He/it guides, leads, shows the way'. The verb means to direct someone toward a goal or along a right path — to lead aright.
6.grammar: A third-person masculine singular present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a 'he/it' subject, and the final long -ī carries the sense 'he guides'. (This verb takes an object directly, 'guides someone', without needing 'to'.)
6.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead aright, show the way

7.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
7.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

8.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
8.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
8.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

9.meaning: 'Say!' — a command to utter or declare something aloud, addressed to a single male.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.
9.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
10.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

11.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
11.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

12.meaning: 'To/for the truth' — al-ḥaqq is that which is real, true, established, and rightfully due: reality as it actually is, the right that is owed, and truth as opposed to falsehood. With the prefix it means 'to the truth' or 'for the truth'.

parts.en: truth / reality / what is rightfully due

12.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') attached to the definite noun al-ḥaqq ('the truth'). The -i ending is genitive, the case regularly required after a preposition such as li-.
12.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, real, established, rightfully due

13.meaning: An interrogative formed from three pieces meaning roughly 'Is then the one who…?' It opens a rhetorical question that compares two parties. The 'a-' is a question marker, 'fa-' links to a preceding statement and means 'then/so', and 'man' is the relative pronoun 'the one who / whoever'.
13.grammar: A combination of particles plus the relative pronoun 'man'. The leading 'a-' turns the sentence into a yes/no question (often rhetorical). 'fa-' is a connective meaning 'then/so', tying the question to what came before. 'man' refers to a person and introduces a clause describing them ('the one who…'); it does not change its ending for case.

14.meaning: 'He/it guides, leads, shows the way'. The verb means to direct someone toward a goal or along a right path — to lead aright.
14.grammar: A third-person masculine singular present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a 'he/it' subject, and the final long -ī carries the sense 'he guides'. (This verb takes an object directly, 'guides someone', without needing 'to'.)
14.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead aright, show the way

15.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
15.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

16.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
16.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
16.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

17.meaning: An adjective meaning 'more entitled, having a better/greater right, more deserving' of something.
17.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the afʿal pattern, meaning 'more/most entitled'. The final -u is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word serves as the subject or as a predicate describing the subject.
17.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, just claim, what is due

18.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
18.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

19.meaning: A present-tense passive verb meaning 'he/it should be followed' or 'is followed' — to be taken as one to walk behind, imitate, and obey. The root sense is coming after, pursuing, and following on the heels of someone.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb in the passive voice ('is/should be followed' rather than 'follows'), shown by the yu- prefix with the internal vowelling. The final -a vowel is the subjunctive/accusative mood-ending, which typically appears after particles meaning 'that', 'so that', or in the answer to a question, giving a sense of 'that he be followed'.
19.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

20.meaning: Or who is it that…? — a compound particle fusing 'or' with 'who,' used to pose a contrasting rhetorical question: 'or rather, who…?'
20.grammar: Two particles merged: am ('or,' used to link question-alternatives) and man ('who,' for persons). Together they introduce a fresh alternative in a rhetorical question, contrasting one claim with another. Neither part inflects.

21.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
21.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

22.meaning: A present/future verb with an object pronoun meaning 'he/it guides me, leads me aright, shows me the way' — to direct someone to the right path and bring them to a goal. The root denotes guidance, right direction, and also a gift offered to lead one toward favour.
22.grammar: An ongoing or future action with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The final -ī is the first-person singular object pronoun ('me'), so the form means 'he guides me'. The verb carries the meaning of leading rightly toward a goal.
22.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, direct to the goal

23.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
23.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

24.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
24.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

25.meaning: A present-tense passive verb meaning 'he/it is guided, is led aright' — to be brought onto the right path by another. The root is guidance and being shown the way.
25.grammar: A present-tense verb in the passive voice ('is guided' rather than 'guides'), marked by the yu- prefix and internal vowelling. The yu- prefix indicates a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it') receiving the action; the final long -ā is the verb's own termination, not a separate morpheme.
25.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, direct to the goal

26.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
26.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

27.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' (plural) — a preposition joined to a pronoun indicating that something belongs to, is owed to, or is directed toward a group of people being addressed.
27.grammar: The preposition la-/li- ('for' or 'to') with the attached pronoun -kum meaning 'you' addressing a group (males or mixed). It expresses possession, benefit, or that something is directed toward the addressees.

28.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
28.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

29.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'you (plural) judge, decide, rule, or pass verdict' — to settle a matter with a binding decision, to govern, and to determine what is right or wrong. The root carries the sense of restraining and wise governance.
29.grammar: An ongoing or future action addressed to a group. The ta-…-ūna frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), giving 'taḥkumūna'. The full -ūna ending (indicative mood) signals a plain, ongoing statement rather than a command or a clause after 'that'.
29.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, govern with wisdom

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'he/it follows, pursues, goes after, conforms to' — to walk behind something, take it as a guide, and obey or imitate it.
2.grammar: An ongoing or future action with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The final -u vowel is the indicative ending, signalling a plain factual statement ('he follows') rather than a command or subjunctive.
2.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

3.meaning: Most of them / the greater part of them — the noun 'akthar' (the greater number, the majority), built on a comparative/superlative pattern of k-th-r ('much/many'), with the pronoun 'them'.
3.grammar: A noun in possessive (genitive) construction: 'aktharu' ('the most of') plus the attached pronoun '-hum' ('them') yields 'most of them'. The '-u' on 'akthar' is the nominative ending, typical when this phrase serves as the subject.
3.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, numerous

4.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
4.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

5.meaning: 'Conjecture, assumption, supposition' — ẓann is a thought or opinion held without certain knowledge: a guess, surmise, or presumption that may be strong but falls short of sure knowledge. The base root spans suspicion, opinion, and supposition.
5.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a conjecture'). The -an ending (written with tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative, often marking the direct object of a verb, an adverbial sense ('by way of conjecture'), or what is specified after certain words.
5.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to suppose, conjecture, think without certainty

6.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
6.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

7.meaning: Conjecture, supposition, opinion not grounded in certainty; a thought or assumption that may be doubt or mere likelihood rather than sure knowledge.
7.grammar: A definite noun: al- is 'the', and the final -a is the accusative ending (fatḥa), which typically marks the word as a direct object of a verb.
7.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — conjecture, supposition, surmise

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'it avails, suffices, benefits, or makes free from need' — to be of use against something or to enrich and relieve someone of need. The root centres on richness, sufficiency, and being free of want.
9.grammar: An ongoing or future action. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), and the form (causative pattern) carries the sense of 'to make sufficient' or 'to be of avail'. The final long -ī is the verb's own weak-root termination.
9.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, sufficient

10.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
10.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

11.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
11.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
11.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

12.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
12.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

13.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
13.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
14.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

15.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
15.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.
15.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, knowing

16.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
16.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

17.meaning: They do / they were doing — a verb of general doing or acting, performing a deed.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb in the basic Form I. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a 3rd-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the -ūna ending is the indicative mood (a plain statement). The verb is the general one for doing, making, or carrying out an action.
17.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — doing, making, performing an act

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
3.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

4.meaning: The Qur'ān — literally 'the Recitation' or 'that which is read aloud'; the name of the revealed Scripture, understood as something recited.
4.grammar: A definite verbal noun ('the recitation') used as a proper name. The final -u is the nominative case, the ending that typically marks the subject or the thing being identified.
4.root: ق-ر-ا (q-r-ʾ) — to read, recite, gather together

5.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
5.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
5.root: — (particle; no root)

6.meaning: A present-tense passive verb meaning 'it is forged, fabricated, or invented falsely' — to be made up as a lie and attributed to someone who did not produce it. The root denotes inventing falsehood and slander.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb in the passive voice ('it is fabricated' rather than 'he fabricates'), shown by the yu- prefix and the form's vowelling. The yu- prefix indicates a third-person masculine singular subject ('it') receiving the action; the final long -ā is the verb's own termination, not a separable morpheme.
6.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to fabricate, invent falsely, forge a lie

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
7.root: — (preposition)

8.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
8.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
8.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
10.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

11.meaning: 'A confirmation, verification, or fulfilment' — taṣdīq is the act of declaring something true and affirming its truth, especially one thing confirming or attesting the truth of another. The root sense is truthfulness and sincerity.
11.grammar: A verbal noun naming the action of confirming as true. The -a ending is accusative, the case commonly used for the direct object of a verb or for what is being predicated/specified ('being a confirmation').
11.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — to be truthful, to affirm as true

12.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
12.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

13.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
13.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
13.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

14.meaning: 'His two hands' — literally a dual 'two hands' with 'his' attached. Often used idiomatically for what lies 'in front of' or 'before' someone (i.e. between his hands).
14.grammar: The noun 'yad' (hand) in its dual form 'two hands'. The -ay ending is the dual in the genitive/accusative state (as opposed to -ā for the subject case), used after prepositions or in possessive links. The attached 'hi' means 'his' (the -i vowel of 'hi' harmonizing after the -ay). In construct, the dual's final -n drops before the pronoun.

15.meaning: 'And a detailed exposition' — tafṣīl is the act of setting something out in full, point by point, distinguishing and clarifying its parts so nothing is left vague. The root means to separate, distinguish, and divide into distinct sections.
15.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a verbal noun naming the action of explaining in full detail. The -a ending is accusative, typically marking a direct object or what is being specified/predicated ('being a detailed exposition').
15.root: ف-ص-ل (f-ṣ-l) — to separate, distinguish, set out in detail

16.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
16.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

17.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
17.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

18.meaning: Doubt, suspicion, disquieting uncertainty — the kind of wavering that unsettles the heart, stronger than a passing question. It names the state of not being at rest about whether something is true.
18.grammar: A masculine singular noun shown with an -a ending and no tanwin. This is the accusative (mansub) noun governed by the negating particle la — its ism — taking a bare form to express absolute negation, conveying that the whole category is ruled out ('there is no doubt whatsoever').

19.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
19.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

20.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
20.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

21.meaning: Lord and Master — the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and has full authority over a thing; a term combining ownership, care, and lordship that goes beyond any single English word.
21.grammar: A noun with the -i (genitive) ending, which typically links the word to a following noun in an 'of / belonging to' relationship, or follows a preposition or oath particle. 'Rabb' denotes a master who owns, sustains, and nurtures what is under his charge.
21.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, mastery and ownership

22.meaning: 'The worlds' or 'all created beings' — al-ʿālamīn refers to every realm and category of created existence (humankind, jinn, angels, all peoples and worlds). It is the all-embracing term for the whole of creation.
22.grammar: A definite sound masculine plural noun. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive or accusative state — the form used after prepositions, when the word is possessed/linked to what precedes ('… OF the worlds'), or as a direct object.
22.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; (related sense) a world/sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

2.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

3.meaning: A past-tense verb with an object pronoun: 'he forged it / invented it falsely' — he fabricated it as a lie and ascribed it to another. The root is the invention of falsehood and slander.
3.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action in the third-person masculine singular ('he forged'), with the attached pronoun -hu ('it/him') as its direct object. The form (built on an added t-) intensifies the sense to deliberate fabrication.
3.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to fabricate, invent falsely, forge a lie

4.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
4.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

5.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'bring!', 'come with!', 'produce!'. From the verb 'to come'; in this pattern with the preposition 'bi-' it means to bring or produce something. Preceded by 'fa-', it reads 'then bring / so produce'.
5.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector signalling a consequence ('then …'). The middle piece is the bare imperative stem of the verb 'to come' (singular '(i)ti'); the '-ū' ending then marks a masculine plural audience ('you all, bring!'). Commands have no case ending. The initial 'i'-sound is a helping vowel that lets the word begin smoothly.
5.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (with bi-) to bring, to produce

6.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'bi-' ('with', and after verbs of bringing, marking the thing brought), joined to 'sūrah', a distinct section or chapter of the Qur'an — literally a unit or 'enclosure' of revelation. Together: 'with a chapter', 'a chapter (to bring)'.
6.grammar: The preposition 'bi-' governs the genitive, which is why 'sūrah' takes the '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr): an indefinite noun in the genitive ('a chapter'). With verbs of bringing, this 'bi-' marks the object one brings.
6.root: س-و-ر (s-w-r) — wall, enclosure; hence a bounded section/chapter

7.meaning: 'Its like, something similar to it, a counterpart of it' — mithl denotes a like, match, or equivalent of a thing, joined here to a pronoun meaning 'of it'. The root sense is likeness, resemblance, and that which is comparable.
7.grammar: A noun meaning 'a like/equivalent' with the attached pronoun -hi ('its/of it'). The -i case-vowel is genitive, the case used after prepositions or when the noun is linked to a following possessor — here joined to the pronoun 'it'.
7.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — to resemble; likeness, similitude, equivalent

8.meaning: A three-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), with a command addressed to a group: 'call!', 'summon!', 'invoke!', or 'invite!'. From the verb 'to call upon'. Together: 'and call upon / and summon'.
8.grammar: 'wa-' connects ('and'). The rest is a command verb to a masculine plural audience; the '-ū' ending marks 'you all' in the imperative. The initial 'i'-sound is a helping vowel that lets the word begin smoothly. Commands take no case ending.
8.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, invite

9.meaning: Who / whoever / the one who. A relative and conditional pronoun used for people, introducing a clause that describes or sets a condition about a person.
9.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun referring to persons; it does not change for case. The final -i is not a case ending but a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting (elidable) alif.

10.meaning: 'You were able / had the capacity / could manage'. From a verb meaning to be capable of something, to have the power or means to do it.
10.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb in the 'seeking/striving' (istaf'ala) pattern, conveying mustering one's ability. The -tum ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject — 'you all' did or could do it.
10.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — willing obedience, capability, being able

11.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
11.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

12.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
12.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
12.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

13.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
13.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

14.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
14.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

15.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
15.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
15.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

16.meaning: The plural of 'ṣādiq': 'truthful ones', 'those who speak the truth', 'the sincere and reliable'. It describes people whose words and conduct match reality.
16.grammar: 'ṣādiq' is an active participle ('one who is truthful'). The '-īna' ending is a 'sound' masculine plural marker; the '-ī-' form (rather than '-ū-') signals that the noun is functioning as an object or is governed by a preposition/particle, while the '-na' completes the plural ('the truthful ones').
16.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, to speak truly

1.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

2.meaning: They denied / they cried lies; they declared (something or someone) to be false. An intensive verb meaning to reject as a lie, to disbelieve and brand untrue — directed by a plural 'they'.

parts.tr: kadhdhab (doubled dh; simplified transliterations may write 'kadhab')
parts.en: denied / branded as lies (past stem, intensive)

2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in an intensive pattern (to treat as false, to repeatedly deny). The middle radical carries a shadda (doubling), which is exactly what marks this as the intensive form: kadhdhab- (not the simple kadhab-). The ending -ū marks the doers as 'they' — a plural, grammatically masculine group, so the whole reconstructs to kadhdhabū. Note that simplified transliterations sometimes omit the doubling and write 'kadhabū', but the doubled dh is essential to the form. The perfect tense denotes a completed action.
2.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this form, to call a lie, to deny as false

3.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
3.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

4.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

4.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

5.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'they encompass, comprehend fully, grasp completely' — to surround something with knowledge so that nothing of it escapes. The root means to surround, enclose, and encircle on every side.
5.grammar: An ongoing or future action with a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The yu- prefix signals third person, while the plural meaning comes from the -ū suffix; together they give 'yuḥīṭū'. The bare -ū (with the final -na dropped) shows the subjunctive/jussive mood, which typically follows particles meaning 'that', 'not yet', or negation/conditions.
5.root: ح-و-ط (ḥ-w-ṭ) — to surround, encompass, enclose on all sides

6.meaning: 'with His knowledge' — by means of, or accompanied by, Allah's own knowledge.
6.grammar: The prefix bi- ('with / by means of') is a preposition. The base is 'knowledge,' and the attached -hi means 'His.' The -i ending on the noun is genitive, the case required after the preposition bi-.

7.meaning: A compound meaning 'and when' — it sets up a circumstance in past time, marking the moment at which something occurred, with the result clause typically following. It carries the sense of 'when, at the time that.'
7.grammar: A particle phrase introducing a past-time clause. Lammā signals 'when' for completed events and expects a following clause stating what then happened; the wa- prefix means 'and.'

8.meaning: It comes to them / reaches them — said of news, a sign, or an event arriving at someone. From the verb 'to come, arrive, reach.'
8.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the 'he/it' form (3rd-person masculine singular). The shortened ending (without a final long vowel) reflects a jussive/subjunctive shape — the form a present verb takes after certain particles (e.g. 'not yet') or in conditions. The attached -him means 'them' (a group of males) as those reached.

9.meaning: Its outcome / interpretation / final fulfilment — the noun 'taʾwīl' (the ultimate meaning, real significance, or eventual realization of a thing) joined to a possessive pronoun, 'its.'
9.grammar: A verbal noun (from form II) with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('its / his'). The -u vowel before the pronoun is the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being talked about.
9.root: ا-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — returning to an origin; hence interpreting, final outcome

10.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
10.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
10.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

11.meaning: A verb meaning 'he denied / cried lies against / rejected as false' — to treat something or someone as a lie, refusing to accept it as true and openly rejecting it.
11.grammar: Past-tense verb (form II, intensive), third-person masculine singular ('he denied / rejected as false'). The doubled middle letter (kadhdhaba) gives the sense of actively declaring something false. The final -a is the past-tense ending for a masculine singular doer.
11.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; (form II) to deny, to call a lie

12.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
12.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: 'Before them' in time — denoting what came earlier, the period or persons preceding a masculine plural group.
14.grammar: An adverb of time, 'before,' carrying the genitive ending -i because it is linked to a following possessor. The attached 'him' means 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group), giving 'before them.' The -i ending reflects that the word is governed in a possessive link.
14.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; before/prior

15.meaning: So look! / then observe! — a command to one person to look at, consider, and reflect upon something.
15.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'you', prefixed by fa- ('so/then'), which links it as a consequence of what precedes. The verb urges one to look and reflect: 'so look!' / 'then consider!'
15.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, see, observe, consider

16.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
16.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

17.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

17.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
17.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

18.meaning: The outcome, end-result, or final consequence — what a matter or a course of conduct ultimately comes to. It names the end that follows from a beginning.
18.grammar: A feminine noun. The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or, without nunation as here, the first term of a possessive phrase ('the outcome of …'). It denotes that which comes at the heel — the consequence that follows on.
18.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow, come after (at the heel); an end, consequence

19.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
19.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

1.meaning: 'And among them / and some of them' — a connective 'and' plus a preposition meaning 'from / among / part of,' joined to the pronoun 'them'; often introduces a subgroup ('among them are …').
1.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') with the preposition min ('from / among'), which always governs a following word in the genitive. Here that word is the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), giving 'and among them / and from them.' Particles like these do not themselves carry case or tense.

2.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

3.meaning: He believes, has faith, trusts securely — to affirm something as true with the heart and place trust in it; an ongoing or characteristic believing.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb in the (āmana) pattern. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine 'he/it' as the doer, and the final -u (unmarked here) indicates the ordinary, unconditioned present ('he believes / does believe').

4.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
4.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

5.meaning: 'And among them / and some of them' — a connective 'and' plus a preposition meaning 'from / among / part of,' joined to the pronoun 'them'; often introduces a subgroup ('among them are …').
5.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') with the preposition min ('from / among'), which always governs a following word in the genitive. Here that word is the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), giving 'and among them / and from them.' Particles like these do not themselves carry case or tense.

6.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
6.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

7.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
7.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

8.meaning: He believes; he has faith. The verb denotes giving heartfelt trust and assent, especially affirming faith in Allah and what He has revealed; the form also carries the sense of granting security.
8.grammar: A present/future verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he' for this verb pattern (form IV), and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain ongoing or habitual statement.

9.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
9.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

10.meaning: 'And your Lord' — joins with 'and' the word rabb, the Master, Sustainer, Owner and Nurturer who creates, provides for and governs His servant, attached to a 'your' (one male).
10.grammar: Noun with 'and' in front and an attached possessor. The -u on rabb is the nominative case, the form a noun takes as a subject or as the thing being named/identified. The suffix -ka means 'your' for a single male.

11.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
11.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.
11.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowing, knowledge

12.meaning: 'Of/with the corrupters / those who spread corruption' — people who cause ruin, disorder, and moral decay, opposed to setting things right.
12.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/of', here often reinforcing a statement), then the definite al- ('the') on an active participle (form IV, 'one who corrupts'). The -ina ending is a sound masculine plural in the genitive case, required after the preposition. It names a class by their action: 'those who spread corruption'.

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: They denied / rejected you — to charge someone with lying, to disbelieve and reject what they say; here a group does this to a single 'you'.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the intensive (form II) pattern, which conveys 'to declare false, treat as a liar'. The suffix '-ū' marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (masculine singular).
2.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; (intensive) to call a lie, deny

3.meaning: So say! / Then say! A command to one person to utter or declare something, introduced by 'so/then.'
3.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so/then,' linking to what precedes. 'Qul' is an imperative (a command) addressed to a single masculine person — 'say!' Its clipped form with a silent final consonant is normal for this command.

4.meaning: For me / to me / mine — a preposition meaning 'to/for' fused with the first-person 'me', expressing possession, benefit, or attribution toward the speaker.
4.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') joined to the attached pronoun -ī ('me'). Together they express that something belongs to, is owed to, or is for the benefit of the speaker.

5.meaning: 'My deed / my work / my action' — ʿamal is a deed, act, or piece of work that one performs, here joined to 'my'. The root denotes doing, working, and acting.
5.grammar: A noun meaning 'deed/work' with the attached possessive pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. The -ī ending is the first-person singular possessive, joining the noun to its owner ('my …').
5.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, perform a deed

6.meaning: A short phrase meaning 'and for you' or 'and you have'. It joins a new statement with 'and', then uses 'for/to you' to express possession or benefit belonging to a group.
6.grammar: Three pieces: wa- ('and') linking to what came before, the preposition la- ('for/to'), and the attached pronoun -kum ('you all', plural). A preposition-plus-'you' phrase like this commonly conveys 'you have' or 'belonging to you'.

7.meaning: 'Your deed / your work / your action' — ʿamal is a deed, act, or piece of work, here joined to 'your' addressing a group. The root denotes doing, working, and acting.
7.grammar: A noun meaning 'deed/work' with the attached possessive pronoun -kum ('your', addressing a group). The -u case-vowel before the pronoun is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or a thing being described ('your deed is …').
7.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, perform a deed

8.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
8.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

9.meaning: 'Free of, quit of, disassociated from' — a plural describing people who are clear, innocent, and dissociated from something, bearing no part in it and no responsibility for it. The root means to be free, clear, cured, and absolved.
9.grammar: A sound masculine plural describing a group ('ones free/quit of …'). The -ūna ending marks the plural in the nominative state — the form used when the word is the subject or is being described ('they are disassociated').
9.root: ب-ر-أ (b-r-ʾ) — to be free, clear, innocent, absolved

10.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
10.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

11.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'I do, I act, I perform' — the first-person form of working or carrying out a deed. The root denotes doing, working, and action.
11.grammar: An ongoing or future action. The a- (hamza) prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'). The final -u vowel is the indicative ending, signalling a plain factual statement ('I do') rather than a command or a clause after 'that'.
11.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, perform a deed

12.meaning: And I — the standalone first-person singular pronoun 'I,' here joined by 'and.' As a detached pronoun it stands on its own (typically as subject), unlike the attached endings.
12.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and.' 'anā' is the independent (detached) pronoun 'I,' used for emphasis or to begin/identify the subject; it does not take a case ending and is fixed in form.

13.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'free of / quit of / disassociated from' — innocent of and having nothing to do with something, washing one's hands of it. It describes a person clear and detached from a thing, especially a wrong.
13.grammar: A descriptive noun, indefinite, with the nominative -un ending (tanwīn). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('[someone] is free/quit'); the -un tanwīn shows it is indefinite. It is usually completed by 'of/from' something.
13.root: ب-ر-ء (b-r-ʾ) — to be free, clear, quit of; innocence, disassociation

14.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
14.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

15.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
15.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: 'And among them / and some of them' — a connective 'and' plus a preposition meaning 'from / among / part of,' joined to the pronoun 'them'; often introduces a subgroup ('among them are …').
1.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') with the preposition min ('from / among'), which always governs a following word in the genitive. Here that word is the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), giving 'and among them / and from them.' Particles like these do not themselves carry case or tense.

2.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

3.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'they listen, give ear, pay attention' — to direct one's hearing toward something attentively, seeking to take it in. The root is hearing and listening; this intensified form adds the sense of deliberately straining to hear.
3.grammar: An ongoing or future action with a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The ya-…-ūna frame marks 'they' (masculine), giving 'yastamiʿūna'; the full -ūna ending (indicative mood) signals a plain, ongoing statement. The added s-t- pattern gives the sense of actively seeking to hear.
3.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — to hear, listen, give ear

4.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
4.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

5.meaning: An emphatic, rhetorical opener combining a question with the sense 'and/then'. It singles out the addressee ('you') and challenges them, roughly 'Is it then YOU who…?' — implying the answer is beyond the person's power.
5.grammar: Built on the question-particle a- ('is it/can it be…?') plus connective fa- ('and/then'), attached to the standalone pronoun anta, 'you' (one male). The pronoun carries no case ending; the fixed final -a is simply part of the word for 'you (masc. sg.)'. The whole expression poses a pointed, rhetorical question focused on the addressee.

6.meaning: To make someone hear, to convey sound to another's ears — and by extension to make a message reach and register with someone, to get through to them.
6.grammar: Present-tense verb of the causative (form IV) pattern, 'to make hear'. The tu- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'), and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain, ongoing or general action ('you make [someone] hear').

7.meaning: Those who cannot hear — the deaf. Often used figuratively for people who refuse to listen to or heed the truth.
7.grammar: A plural noun/adjective with the definite article al- ('the'). The l of al- assimilates into the following ṣ (a 'sun letter'), so it is pronounced ṣ-ṣumma. The final -a is the accusative ending, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('the deaf ones' as the thing acted upon).
7.root: ص-م-م (ṣ-m-m) — deafness, being unhearing

8.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
8.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

9.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
9.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

10.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
10.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

11.meaning: 'They understand / use reason.' To comprehend, reason, and grasp things with the intellect — to 'tie down' meaning with the mind, to think rationally and exercise sound judgment.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame means 'they [do]' for a group of males or a mixed group. The full -ūna ending (with the final -na intact) marks the indicative mood, i.e. a plain factual statement. The root sense is binding/restraining, hence using the mind to 'hold' meaning.
11.root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l) — to bind, restrain; intellect, reason

3.meaning: To look, to see, to direct one's gaze or attention toward something; also to wait for or consider.
3.grammar: Present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), and the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain, ongoing or habitual action ('he looks / is looking').

4.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.

6.meaning: To guide, to lead someone along the right way, to show the path to truth or to a goal — a directing toward what is correct.
6.grammar: Present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The verb ends in a long -ī because its root's final letter is a weak (vowel-like) letter; this final-weak shape is the normal indicative form here, marking a plain ongoing or general action ('you guide').

7.meaning: Those who cannot see — the blind. Frequently used figuratively for people blind to the truth, unable or unwilling to perceive guidance.
7.grammar: A plural noun/adjective with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative ending, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('the blind ones' as the thing acted upon).
7.root: ع-م-ي (ʿ-m-y) — blindness, loss of sight

8.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
8.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

11.meaning: To see, perceive with the eyes, or have insight — to look and take in, with a nuance of clear perception and understanding, not mere glancing. Used of a group: 'they see / perceive'.
11.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they see'). The yu- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks an ongoing or repeated action done by a group of males or a mixed group. The -ūna ending is the 'indicative' form used when the verb is not preceded by something that would shorten it.
11.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — sight, seeing, insight

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
2.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: He wrongs or deals unjustly — to commit injustice, to put something out of its right place, or to deprive another of what is due.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular doing something now or habitually ('he wrongs'), and the final '-u' marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact rather than a command or a subjunctive/jussive form.
4.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression; misplacing a thing

5.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
5.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
5.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

6.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
6.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

7.meaning: A connective particle 'but / however / yet' used to correct or contrast with what precedes, here with emphasis. It introduces a clause that sets the record straight against an expectation.
7.grammar: A contrastive conjunction ('but, however') joined by 'wa' ('and'). This is the heavy, emphatic form 'lākinna', which governs the noun after it into the object ('-a') case and adds force, like saying 'but in fact …'. It rebuts or qualifies a preceding statement.
7.root: — (no triliteral root; a compound particle of exception/contrast)

8.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
8.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
8.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
9.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.
9.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, person; breath

10.meaning: 'They wrong / they do wrong' — to act unjustly or oppressively, presented as an ongoing or repeated action. The same root pictures putting things out of their proper place.
10.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a plural masculine 'they' doing the action now or habitually ('they wrong / keep wronging'). The full -ūna ending (with its final -na) is the mark of the ordinary, uninterrupted present tense for a plural subject.

1.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
1.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'He gathers them' or 'He will assemble them' — to collect and herd people together into one place, as in the great mustering of creation.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The stem-final -u is the indicative mood, marking a plain statement of fact (and, of future events, what will certainly occur). The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (masculine plural).
2.root: ح-ش-ر (ḥ-sh-r) — to gather, herd together, muster

3.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'as if / as though.' It introduces a comparison or likeness, treating a situation as resembling another — presenting something as if it were a certain way, whether or not it truly is.
3.grammar: A particle of comparison formed from 'ka-' ('like / as') joined to a particle meaning 'that.' Together they function as a single linking word, 'as if,' used to liken one circumstance to another. It is a particle, so it has no case ending of its own.

4.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
4.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

5.meaning: To stay, to remain, to linger or tarry in a place for a span of time.
5.grammar: Present-tense verb with a third-person masculine plural subject: the ya- prefix plus the -ū ending together mean 'they (men/people).' The plain indicative would end in -ūna; here the shortened -ū (with a silent written alif) shows the verb is in a dependent mood — the form used after certain particles or in negation, e.g. 'they did not remain / that they remain.'
5.root: ل-ب-ث (l-b-th) — staying, tarrying, abiding

6.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
6.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

7.meaning: An hour; more broadly a span of time, a moment, or the appointed 'Hour' (the climactic moment of resurrection and judgement). Its underlying sense is a defined stretch or point of time.
7.grammar: A feminine noun in the indefinite accusative. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('an hour, some hour') and as accusative — the case used for the direct object of a verb or for adverbial expressions of time and extent (e.g. 'for an hour').
7.root: س-و-ع (s-w-ʿ) — a moment or span of time

8.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
8.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

9.meaning: The daytime — the bright span of hours when the sun is up, from dawn to sunset; the natural counterpart of night.
9.grammar: A definite singular noun (the 'al-' prefix means 'the,' with its 'l' assimilated into the following 'n'). The final '-i' is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding noun ('… OF the day') or as following a preposition or a particle that governs the genitive.
9.root: ن-ه-ر (n-h-r) — daylight, flowing/spreading open

10.meaning: To recognize one another, to come to know each other mutually — people identifying and acknowledging one another.
10.grammar: Present-tense verb of the mutual/reciprocal (form VI) pattern, 'to know one another.' The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The full -ūna ending is the plain indicative, marking an ongoing or future action ('they recognize one another').

11.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
11.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
11.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

12.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
12.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

13.meaning: 'he lost / suffered loss' — to forfeit or be deprived of something of value, ending in ruin or deficit; the opposite of profit and gain.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular: 'he lost / has lost.' The final -a is the standard ending marking a completed action done by 'he.'
13.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — loss, ruin, to be a loser

14.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
14.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

15.meaning: They denied / they cried lies; they declared (something or someone) to be false. An intensive verb meaning to reject as a lie, to disbelieve and brand untrue — directed by a plural 'they'.

parts.tr: kadhdhab (doubled dh; simplified transliterations may write 'kadhab')
parts.en: denied / branded as lies (past stem, intensive)

15.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in an intensive pattern (to treat as false, to repeatedly deny). The middle radical carries a shadda (doubling), which is exactly what marks this as the intensive form: kadhdhab- (not the simple kadhab-). The ending -ū marks the doers as 'they' — a plural, grammatically masculine group, so the whole reconstructs to kadhdhabū. Note that simplified transliterations sometimes omit the doubling and write 'kadhabū', but the doubled dh is essential to the form. The perfect tense denotes a completed action.
15.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this form, to call a lie, to deny as false

16.meaning: A noun meaning 'a meeting, encounter, or coming face-to-face,' prefixed with 'in/with.' It denotes the act of two parties meeting, often used for the encounter with one's Lord.

parts.en: genitive ending (because of the preceding preposition)
