2.meaning: A rhetorical address meaning roughly 'Have you considered?' or 'Tell me — what do you think of…?'. It combines the question particle 'a-' ('do/have…?') with the verb 'to see', here in the sense of mentally considering or reflecting on something rather than literal eyesight. It is addressed to a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: A past-tense verb carrying a subject built into its ending: the '-tum' ending marks a completed action done by 'you all' (masculine plural). Prefixed with the question particle 'a-', it turns the statement into a question, idiomatically 'have you considered / tell me'.

3.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
3.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

4.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
4.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
5.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
5.root: — (proper divine name)

6.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
6.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

7.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
7.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

8.meaning: 'Provision, sustenance' — rizq is whatever Allah bestows that benefits a creature: food, wealth, and every good thing one is granted to live on.
8.grammar: A singular indefinite noun with the -in ending, which is the genitive with tanwīn. The genitive typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('some of (the) provision …').
8.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — provision, sustenance, that which is bestowed to live on

9.meaning: 'Then you (all) made / appointed / rendered' — from jaʿala, a versatile verb meaning to make, to set in place, to designate something as such, or to begin.
9.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The -tum ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject: 'you (all) did (it).' The prefixed fa- means 'then/so', linking to what precedes.
9.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, appoint, render, bring about

10.meaning: A prepositional phrase, 'from him/it' — indicating origin or source, that something proceeds out of him/it.
10.grammar: The preposition min ('from') with the attached pronoun -hu ('him/it', third-person masculine singular). As the object of a preposition the pronoun stands in the genitive; the combination indicates source or origin.

11.meaning: 'Forbidden, unlawful, sacred and off-limits' — ḥarām is that which is prohibited and set apart so as not to be violated; the same root yields the sense of the sacred and inviolable.
11.grammar: A singular indefinite noun/adjective with the -an ending, which is the accusative with tanwīn. The accusative commonly marks a direct object or a description of one ('made [it] forbidden').
11.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — prohibition, sacredness, inviolability; that which is set off-limits

12.meaning: 'And lawful, permitted' — ḥalāl is that which is allowed and released for use, the opposite of what is forbidden.
12.grammar: A singular indefinite noun/adjective with the -an ending (accusative with tanwīn), which commonly marks a direct object or a description of one ('made [it] lawful'). The opening wa- is the conjunction 'and'.
12.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to be lawful/permitted; to untie, release, make allowable; to alight

13.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
13.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

14.meaning: 'Is it Allah (who)…?' — the proper name of the One True God, here opened by an interrogative hamza turning it into a question ('Allah — is it He…?'). Allah is the unique, personal name of the Divine.
14.grammar: A proper name with the -u ending (nominative), which typically marks the subject of a sentence ('Allah [did/is] …'). The lengthened opening hamza (ā-) is the interrogative particle merged with the article of the name, turning the word into a question.

15.meaning: 'He gave permission / allowed / sanctioned' — from adhina, to permit and authorize; the same root carries the sense of giving ear and heeding.
15.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject: 'he did (it).' It denotes an action viewed as finished.
15.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, allow, authorize; to give ear, listen, heed

16.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
16.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

17.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

17.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.
17.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

18.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
18.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
18.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

19.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
19.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

20.meaning: You fabricate or invent falsehood — to forge a lie deliberately, weaving something untrue and attributing it falsely. The verb carries the sense of concocting and slandering against truth.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb in form VIII. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural ('you all') in the ongoing/habitual mode — an action presently happening or repeatedly done.
20.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to fabricate, forge, invent (especially a lie)

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: An assumption, conjecture, or supposition — an opinion or belief held without certainty. It spans a range from mere guesswork and doubt to a strong, settled presumption, depending on context.
2.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('the assumption is …').

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: They fabricate or invent falsely — to forge a lie, concoct something untrue and attribute it where it does not belong. The verb specifically names inventing falsehood and slander out of nothing.
4.grammar: Present-tense verb in the (form VIII) pattern, third-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks the third person and, together with the -ūna ending, yields 'they' (masculine plural) acting in ongoing/present time. The retained -na is the mark of the indicative ('they are fabricating / they fabricate').

5.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
5.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
5.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'the lie / falsehood' — a deliberate untruth, a fabricated statement that contradicts reality.
7.grammar: A definite masculine noun with the prefix al- ('the'). The final -a marks the accusative case, which most commonly identifies the noun as the direct object — the thing upon which an action (such as saying or inventing) falls.
7.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, to be false, to deny the truth

8.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
8.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
8.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

9.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
9.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.
9.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise

10.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
10.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
11.root: — (proper name)

12.meaning: An emphatic statement that someone is truly the holder or owner of something. The opening lām is a particle of emphasis ('surely/indeed'), and dhū means 'owner of, possessor of, the one endowed with' — it is a word that always governs a following noun to say someone is rich in or characterized by that thing.
12.grammar: The la- prefix is the 'lām of emphasis' that strengthens a statement ('indeed, surely'). Dhū is one of the special 'five nouns'; its long -ū ending marks the nominative (subject) case, the form used when this word is the doer or the thing being described, and it must be followed by a noun in the genitive ('possessor OF …').

13.meaning: Bounty, grace, favor; an overflowing generosity or surplus given freely. It denotes goodness and abundance bestowed beyond what is owed or expected, and by extension excellence or superiority.
13.grammar: The -in ending is genitive plus 'tanwīn' (the -n indicating indefiniteness, 'a bounty'). The genitive case typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF bounty') or follows a preposition.
13.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — bounty, grace, excess goodness, superiority

14.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
14.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
14.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

15.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
15.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
15.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

16.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
16.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.

17.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'most of them / the greater part of them' — the larger portion of a group.
17.grammar: An elative/comparative noun ('more/most, the greater number') on the 'afʿal' pattern. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form used when the word is a verb's object. The attached -hum ('them') is in the possessive role, completing the sense 'the most of them'.
17.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — muchness, abundance, being many

18.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
18.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

19.meaning: They give thanks — to be grateful, to acknowledge and appreciate a benefit or blessing and respond to its giver with thankfulness, often expressed in word and deed.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject ('they'), and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural in the ongoing/habitual mode — an action happening now or done regularly.
19.root: ش-ك-ر (sh-k-r) — to thank, to be grateful

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: It is / it will be / so as to be — a verb of 'being', expressing existence or a state of being.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person feminine singular ('it', e.g. a feminine thing). The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it' as the subject. The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain statement of being. From a hollow root whose middle و appears as the long ū.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: An affair, matter, state, or situation — a circumstance or concern that occupies one. It denotes a condition or piece of business of significance, the 'thing one is engaged in'.
4.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The -in ending combines the genitive case with indefiniteness ('a/an'); the genitive typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun, while the final -n (nunation) signals 'some, any' rather than a specific one.

5.meaning: A compound: the connective 'and' joined to the particle mā. The particle mā is highly versatile — it can mean 'what / whatever' (introducing an indirect question or a relative clause, 'that which'), or it can function as a negation ('not'). Context determines which sense applies; the core idea is an open, unspecified 'what(ever)' or a flat denial.
5.grammar: Two indeclinable particles, so there is no case ending to mark. The wa- prefix is the simple connective 'and', linking what follows to what precedes. Mā itself does not change form: it serves either as an interrogative/relative ('what, that which') or as a negating word ('not').

6.meaning: You all recite / they (fem.) recite — the present-tense act of reciting aloud, reading out, or rehearsing words in sequence (especially scripture), addressed to a male plural group ('you all') or done by a female plural subject ('they').
6.grammar: Present/imperfect tense. The 'ta-' prefix together with the '-ū' plural suffix marks either a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all recite') or a third-person feminine plural ('they recite'); a feminine singular reading is ruled out because the '-ū' suffix is plural. The ending '-ū' (without final 'na') is the shortened subjunctive/jussive mood, used after certain particles or in dependent clauses. The verb means 'recite/read out in sequence'.
6.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read out, follow in sequence

7.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
7.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
7.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: A recitation — that which is recited or read aloud; the verbal noun naming the act and the recited text itself. As a proper term it designates the revealed Scripture, 'the Recitation'.
9.grammar: A masculine verbal noun. The -in ending marks the genitive case together with indefiniteness ('a recitation'); the genitive typically follows a preposition or attaches the word to a preceding noun, and the final -n (nunation) signals 'some, any'.
9.root: ق-ر-أ (q-r-ʾ) — to read, to recite

10.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
10.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

11.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
11.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

12.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
12.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

13.meaning: A deed, work, or action — something done or performed, an act of doing whether good or bad. It is the concrete fruit of effort and intent put into action.
13.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The -in ending marks the genitive case with indefiniteness ('a deed'); the genitive typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun, and the final -n (nunation) conveys 'some, any'.
13.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, to work, to act

14.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
14.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

15.meaning: 'We were' — the past tense of the verb 'to be,' establishing a past state or condition for a group including the speaker. It is the basic verb of existence and of 'being something.'
15.grammar: The past tense of 'to be' in the first-person plural ('we were'). The subject suffix is -nā ('we'); its nūn is written with a shadda (نَّ) because it merges with the final nūn of the verb stem kun-, and the alif spells the long -ā. A hollow verb, its middle weak letter drops in this form. It sets up a past state, and what follows describes how 'we' were.
15.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being, existence

16.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
16.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

17.meaning: Witnesses — those present and observing, who can testify to what they have seen or known. The plural denotes a group bearing witness or attending to an event.
17.grammar: A masculine plural noun. The -an ending marks the accusative case with indefiniteness; the accusative commonly marks the object of a verb or a descriptive state ('as witnesses'), and the final -n (nunation) signals 'some, any'.
17.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, to be present, to testify

18.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
18.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

19.meaning: You pour forth or plunge into — to surge and spread into an activity, especially to launch eagerly into talk or discourse, immersing oneself in a matter as a flood spills over.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb in form IV. The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural ('you all') in the ongoing mode — an action happening now or habitually.
19.root: ف-ي-ض (f-y-ḍ) — to overflow, pour forth, abound

20.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
20.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

21.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
21.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

22.meaning: It is hidden from, escapes, or is absent from — to be remote and concealed, slipping away beyond reach or notice. It conveys something being out of sight or out of one's awareness.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), and the -u ending marks the indicative mood — a plain factual statement of something ongoing or generally true.
22.root: ع-ز-ب (ʿ-z-b) — to be far off, absent, hidden

23.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

23.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

24.meaning: The Lord belonging to a single male 'you' — Rabb is the Master, Owner, and Sustainer who creates, nurtures, and brings to maturity; here 'your Lord'.
24.grammar: The noun rabb (Lord, Sustainer) with the attached pronoun -ka, 'your' for one male. The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, the case that typically links a word to a following possessor or follows a preposition (here showing the possession 'of you'). The doubled b (shadda) belongs to the root.

25.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
25.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

26.meaning: The weight or measure of — the heaviness of a thing used as a standard of comparison, as in 'the weight of …'. It denotes an exact quantity, even a tiny one, against which something is measured.
26.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The -i ending is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a following noun ('the weight OF …') or follows a preposition.

27.meaning: A tiny particle — a mote, a speck of dust, the smallest ant; proverbially the least conceivable amount of matter.
27.grammar: A singular noun (the unit-noun of 'specks'). The final '-in' (tanwīn kasra) marks the indefinite genitive — 'of a speck' — the form a noun takes when it follows another noun in a possessive pairing or comes after a preposition.
27.root: ذ-ر-ر (dh-r-r) — minute particles; motes of dust scattered in the air

28.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
28.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

29.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
29.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

30.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
30.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

31.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
31.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

32.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
32.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

33.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
33.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

34.meaning: Smaller, lesser, or tinier — the comparative/superlative form expressing 'more small' or 'smallest'. It marks something diminished in size or significance relative to another.
34.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the pattern aCCaC ('more/most …'). The final -a ending is accusative, which commonly marks an object or follows certain particles; this form is diptote and does not take nunation. It expresses 'smaller / smallest'.

35.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
35.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

36.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
36.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

37.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
37.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

38.meaning: Comparative/superlative adjective: 'greater, bigger' or 'greatest, biggest.' Built on the 'more/most' pattern from the root sense of largeness, weight, or importance.
38.grammar: An elative adjective (the 'more / most' pattern, like 'greater'). The final '-a' is the accusative case ending: it typically marks the word as the object of a verb, or as a descriptive complement, and is also the case this fixed (diptote) pattern takes where others would show '-i'.
38.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great, large, weighty

39.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
39.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

40.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
40.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

41.meaning: A Book, a scripture — a written record or revealed text. In sacred usage it denotes a divinely revealed Scripture. The indefinite form means 'a book / some scripture' rather than a specific one.
41.grammar: A noun. The final -in (tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive ending: it marks the word as indefinite ('a book') and in the genitive case, the case typically used after a preposition or when one noun is linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
41.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; 'kitāb' = something written, a book

42.meaning: Means 'clear / plain / making manifest' — something that is evident in itself and also makes other things plain, leaving no ambiguity.
42.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) from a pattern that often carries the sense 'making clear' as well as 'being clear.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite), the form taken after a preposition or when describing a genitive noun — i.e. it agrees with a preceding indefinite noun in the genitive ('a clear …').
42.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct; to make evident

1.meaning: An opening particle of alert and emphasis — 'Now then!', 'Beware!', 'Truly!'. It calls attention to and strongly affirms the statement that follows.
1.grammar: An attention-drawing particle placed at the start of a statement. It rouses the listener and emphasizes what comes next, somewhat like 'Indeed!', 'Lo!', or 'Take note!' in English.

2.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
2.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

3.meaning: Allies, protectors, intimate friends — those taken as close supporters, patrons, or guardians, with whom one stands in mutual loyalty (plural of walī).
3.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'walī.' Being a 'diptote' (a noun that resists the usual full set of endings), it takes a single final '-a' here for the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb or signals 'as / being' something — and notably without the usual '-n' (no nunation).

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

6.meaning: 'Fear' — a state of being afraid, dread, or alarm; apprehension of something harmful or threatening.
6.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as nominative and indefinite — 'a fear' or simply 'fear' — and the nominative typically signals the doer or subject of a sentence, or the subject of an existential statement ('there is fear').

7.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
7.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
7.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

8.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

9.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
9.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

10.meaning: 'They grieve / will grieve' — to feel sorrow, sadness, or distress; to be saddened over loss or hardship.
10.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine plural. The 'ya-' prefix marks third person, and the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') with the verb in its full (indicative) form, describing ongoing or future action. Read together the word is 'yaḥzanūna.'

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
2.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

3.meaning: A compound meaning 'and they were' or 'and they used to' — it sets a state or habit in the past. The verb 'to be/become' here establishes an ongoing past condition, often paired with a following verb to express habitual action.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb ('to be') in the third-person masculine plural — the -ū ending means 'they' did/were. It commonly conveys a continued past state or habit, especially when followed by another verb. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

4.meaning: They are mindful of Allah / they guard themselves; to live in reverent awareness that shields one from wrongdoing (the verb behind taqwā).
4.grammar: A Form VIII present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame means 'they (do)' for a group of males, with the final -na marking the indicative mood — a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual reality.
4.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to protect, shield, guard against harm

1.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
1.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

2.meaning: The glad tidings — good news, joyful announcement of something pleasing. The word names the very message of joy that brings cheer and makes the face brighten.
2.grammar: A feminine noun carrying the definite article al- ('the'). It ends in a fixed long -ā (the feminine pattern fuʿlā) which does not change for case, so the case is understood from context rather than a final short vowel.
2.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — to bring good news, to rejoice

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: 'The life' — living existence, the state of being alive.
4.grammar: The definite article al- with the feminine noun ḥayāt ('life'); the waw belongs to the stem and the tā' marbūṭa is its feminine suffix. The final -i is the genitive case vowel, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a following noun.

5.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
5.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
5.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

6.meaning: 'And in' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'in / within / during.'
6.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the preposition fī ('in'). Fī governs the following noun, putting it into the genitive case. Neither particle changes form.

7.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
7.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
7.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: Alteration or substitution — the act of changing one thing for another, replacing or modifying. The verbal noun names the process of exchange or transformation.
9.grammar: A masculine verbal noun of form II. The -a ending marks the accusative case, which commonly marks the object of a verb and is also the form used after the absolute-negation particle ('no change at all').
9.root: ب-د-ل (b-d-l) — to change, exchange, replace

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'the words / utterances / decrees,' prefixed with 'for/to.' Beyond ordinary speech it can denote Allah's words, commands, and decisive decrees. It is the plural of 'word.'

parts.en: genitive ending (because of the preceding preposition)

10.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun governed by the attached preposition li- ('for / to'). The final -i is the genitive case ending — the form sound feminine plurals take after a preposition or when linked to a following noun ('… of …').
10.root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m) — to speak; hence a word or utterance

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
12.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

13.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
13.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

14.meaning: 'The success' / 'the triumph' — attainment of what is sought and safety from what is feared; winning, salvation, the great achievement. With the article it is 'the (true) success'.
14.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -u ending is the nominative case, marking it as a subject or as the thing identified (e.g. 'that IS the success').
14.root: ف-و-ز (f-w-z) — to win, triumph, attain salvation

15.meaning: 'the Most Great / the Immense' — vast, mighty, and tremendous in greatness and grandeur. As a divine name it conveys overwhelming magnificence and majesty.
15.grammar: A definite adjective/noun in an intensive pattern ('the Magnificent'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for an appositive descriptive title attached to such a subject.
15.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'it grieves you' or 'it makes you sad' — to cause sorrow, distress, or anxiety to a single addressee.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it') marked by the 'ya-' prefix. The vowel-less (jussive) ending on the stem shows it follows a governing particle such as a negative or conditional. The attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (one male).

3.meaning: Their saying, statement, or word; what they say. The verbal noun qawl means an utterance or speech-act, here marked as belonging to a group.
3.grammar: A verbal noun ('saying / speech') with the possessive pronoun -hum ('their') attached, so 'their saying.' The -u vowel before the pronoun is the nominative ending: it typically marks the word as the subject or topic of a sentence. The pronoun -hum refers to a masculine plural group ('them/their').

4.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
4.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

5.meaning: Might, honour, and unassailable strength; the quality of being mighty and held in high esteem, beyond reach of humiliation.
5.grammar: A definite singular noun ('the might/honour'). The -ta ending (the t of the feminine ending plus an -a) is accusative, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case.
5.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, dearness, being unassailable

6.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
6.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

7.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
7.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.
7.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — gathering, joining, bringing together

8.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
8.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

9.meaning: "the All-Hearing" — one who hears, perceiving all sounds completely and constantly; used as a divine name it denotes the One whose hearing is perfect and all-encompassing.
9.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, which conveys a deep, enduring quality ('ever-hearing,' not merely 'hearing once'). The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form a word takes when it is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.
9.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — hearing, listening

10.meaning: The All-Knowing — one whose knowledge is complete, perfect, and all-encompassing; an intensive form stressing that knowing is an essential, constant attribute.
10.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that stresses depth and permanence of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

1.grammar: An attention-drawing particle placed at the start of a statement. It rouses the listener and emphasizes what comes next, somewhat like 'Indeed!', 'Lo!', or 'Take note!' in English.

2.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
2.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

3.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
3.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

4.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
4.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
5.root: — (particle)

6.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
6.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

7.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
7.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
7.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').
9.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

10.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

11.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'he/it follows, pursues, goes after, conforms to' — to walk behind something, take it as a guide, and obey or imitate it.
11.grammar: An ongoing or future action with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The final -u vowel is the indicative ending, signalling a plain factual statement ('he follows') rather than a command or subjunctive.
11.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

12.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
12.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

13.meaning: 'They call / invite / summon' — to call upon, invite, or summon (also to pray to or call out to); a present-tense verb with a masculine-plural subject.
13.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they call/invite'). The ya- prefix with the full -ūna ending marks 'they (men) do' and shows the indicative mood — the plain statement form ('they do'), with its final nūn intact (contrast the jussive/subjunctive, where it drops).
13.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, pray

14.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
14.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

15.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
15.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
15.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

16.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
16.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

17.meaning: Associates, partners, or co-sharers — those set up as participants alongside another in ownership, authority, or worship. In theological usage it denotes rivals falsely placed beside Allah.
17.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of sharīk ('partner'), following the pattern faʿalāʾ. This pattern is a diptote, so it takes no nunation. The word is in the accusative case, marked by the short -a vowel on the word-final hamzah (آءَ); that hamzah is part of the plural pattern itself and cannot be split off as a separate ending. The accusative is the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('they made/claimed partners') or after certain particles.
17.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partake, associate

18.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
18.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

19.meaning: They follow, pursue, or go after (something), tracking its path closely; from a verb meaning to follow in succession.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form VIII) with the ya- prefix marking a third-person subject. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') in the indicative mood, the form used for a plain, ongoing statement of fact.

20.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
20.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

21.meaning: Conjecture, supposition, opinion not grounded in certainty; a thought or assumption that may be doubt or mere likelihood rather than sure knowledge.
21.grammar: A definite noun: al- is 'the', and the final -a is the accusative ending (fatḥa), which typically marks the word as a direct object of a verb.

22.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
22.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

23.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
23.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

24.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
24.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

25.meaning: They guess, conjecture, or speak from mere estimation; from a verb meaning to surmise or speak falsely without sound basis.
25.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I) with the ya- prefix. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') in the indicative mood, used for an ongoing or habitual statement.
25.root: خ-ر-ص (kh-r-ṣ) — to conjecture, estimate, speak by guesswork

1.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
1.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: 'He made,' 'He appointed,' 'He set up' — to bring about, fashion, or assign something to a state or role. Beyond mere 'making,' it often means rendering one thing into another or establishing something for a purpose.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer and places the action in the completed past ('he made / appointed'). This verb commonly governs two objects, in the sense of 'made X into Y.'

4.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something is done or given.
4.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). Such prepositions assign a benefit, purpose, or recipient. The pronoun's vowel appears as '-u' (kumu) to ease pronunciation when a word follows.

5.meaning: The night — al-layl is the period of darkness from sunset to dawn; the dark portion of the day-night cycle, a time of covering, rest and stillness.
5.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative case, the ending typically given to the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or used adverbially for time ('the night').
5.root: ل-ي-ل (l-y-l) — night, darkness

6.meaning: So that you may find rest and stillness — to settle down, grow calm, and dwell at ease, the restlessness quieted into repose and tranquil dwelling.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb preceded by li- ('so that, in order to'), which expresses purpose and puts the verb in the subjunctive. The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the -ū ending marks masculine plural ('you all') — note the subjunctive after li- drops the final -na.
6.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to be still, to rest, to dwell

7.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
7.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

8.meaning: And the daytime — the period of daylight between dawn and sunset, the bright span of the day as opposed to night.
8.grammar: A masculine noun with the prefix wa- ('and') and the definite article (here assimilated as n-nahār). The final -a ending is the accusative case, which commonly marks the object of a verb or the thing being pointed to.

9.meaning: Giving light to see by — making things visible, illuminating so that sight is possible. The active participle describes something that grants visibility or causes one to see clearly.
9.grammar: An active participle of form IV (the mu- prefix marks 'the one doing/causing the action'). The -an ending marks the accusative with indefiniteness, commonly used for a descriptive state ('as something giving light'), and the final -n (nunation) signals 'a/some'.
9.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — to see, to perceive, sight

10.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
10.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
11.root: — (particle)

12.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
12.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

13.meaning: Surely signs, tokens, or clear indications; evidences that point to a greater truth. The prefixed lām adds emphasis ('surely / indeed').
13.grammar: An emphatic particle 'la-' ('surely') joined to an indefinite feminine plural noun ('signs'). The -āt- is the sound feminine plural marker; the final -in (nunation) marks it indefinite. For this plural pattern the -in form serves for both the accusative and the genitive case.

14.meaning: For a people, for a folk or community; a group of human beings considered together. Joined to the preposition 'li' ('for / to').
14.grammar: The preposition 'li' ('for / to') plus an indefinite singular noun ('a people'). The -in ending (nunation) marks indefiniteness; it is the genitive form, required because nouns governed by 'li' stand in the genitive.
14.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people/community

15.meaning: 'They hear / listen' — a present-tense verb for hearing sounds, and by extension listening or heeding.
15.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' hearing now or habitually. The full -ūna ending shows the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state.
15.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — to hear, listen, heed

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'he took (for himself), adopted, or acquired' — to take something and make it one's own; from a reflexive pattern implying taking to oneself.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) Form VIII verb, third-person masculine singular ('he took'). Form VIII often carries a reflexive sense (taking for oneself). The final -a is the standard perfect ending, marking a completed act. The initial alif is a connecting hamza, sounded only at the start of an utterance.

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: The noun 'child, son, or offspring' — what is born of someone; can denote a son specifically or progeny generally.
4.grammar: A masculine noun with the ending '-an' (tanwīn), the indefinite accusative — the case typical of a direct object ('a child' as the thing taken/had). The final alif is the spelling support for this '-an' ending.
4.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to beget, give birth; child, offspring

5.meaning: An exclamation of glorification meaning 'far removed and utterly above all imperfection is He.' The verbal noun 'subḥān' declares that the One referred to is exalted beyond any deficiency, partner, or fault, and the attached 'Him' directs that declaration to a single masculine being.
5.grammar: A verbal noun used as an absolute exclamation, fixed in the accusative ending -a (an emphatic declaration, roughly 'I declare His utter transcendence'). The attached -hu is the possessive/object pronoun 'Him', referring to one masculine person.
5.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide away, hence to declare Allah free of all imperfection

6.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
6.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

7.meaning: The Self-Sufficient / the Free-of-Need / the Rich — the One utterly independent and in need of nothing, possessing all wealth; as a human trait it means rich or free from want.
7.grammar: An intensive adjective on the 'faʿīl' pattern (denoting a deep, established quality), with 'the'. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as a subject or the thing being described.
7.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, self-sufficient

8.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
8.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

9.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
9.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
11.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.
11.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, sky

12.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
12.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
14.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

15.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
15.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

16.meaning: In your possession, presence, or keeping; available to you. The base word 'ʿinda' denotes being at, near, or held by someone, whether physically present or stored as knowledge or property.
16.grammar: An adverb of place meaning 'with/at', fixed in the accusative ('-a'), joined to the pronoun '-kum' ('you', for a group). Together it locates something as being present with or belonging to a group of people.

17.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
17.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

18.meaning: 'Authority, warrant, sanction' — a proof or sanctioning power that gives one the right to make a claim; can mean compelling evidence or delegated authority/dominion.
18.grammar: A noun. The '-in' (tanwīn kasra) marks it indefinite ('any authority/proof') and in the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or in an 'of' linkage. It commonly denotes both a sanctioning proof and ruling power.
