19.meaning: A prepositional phrase meaning 'by this' or 'with this' — the preposition 'with/by means of' joined to the demonstrative 'this', pointing to something near or just mentioned.
19.grammar: A preposition bi- ('with', 'by') attached to the demonstrative pronoun hādhā ('this', masculine singular). The demonstrative is invariable in form here; the preposition indicates instrument or means ('by means of this') or association ('with this').

20.meaning: A question 'Do you (plural) say…?' — challenging or asking a group whether they assert or claim something, in the present tense.
20.grammar: An interrogative particle 'a-' ('do…?') prefixed to a present-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all') in the indicative (ongoing action); the leading 'a-' turns the statement into a question.

21.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
21.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
21.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

22.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
22.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

23.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
23.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

24.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
24.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

25.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
25.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
2.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: They fabricate or invent falsely — to forge a lie, concoct something untrue and attribute it where it does not belong. The verb specifically names inventing falsehood and slander out of nothing.
4.grammar: Present-tense verb in the (form VIII) pattern, third-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks the third person and, together with the -ūna ending, yields 'they' (masculine plural) acting in ongoing/present time. The retained -na is the mark of the indicative ('they are fabricating / they fabricate').

5.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
5.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
5.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'the lie / falsehood' — a deliberate untruth, a fabricated statement that contradicts reality.
7.grammar: A definite masculine noun with the prefix al- ('the'). The final -a marks the accusative case, which most commonly identifies the noun as the direct object — the thing upon which an action (such as saying or inventing) falls.
7.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, to be false, to deny the truth

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: They prosper, succeed, or attain salvation — to achieve well-being and lasting success, to win what is sought and be saved from loss. It carries the sense of flourishing and ultimate triumph.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb in form IV. The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject ('they'), and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural in the ongoing/habitual mode — an action presently true or generally the case.
9.root: ف-ل-ح (f-l-ḥ) — to prosper, succeed, attain

1.meaning: Provision, enjoyment, or maintenance; a beneficial gift of goods, comfort, or sustenance that one is given to make use of, typically for a limited time.
1.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamm) marks the indefinite nominative — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for the thing being stated to exist ('there is a provision').
1.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — to provide enjoyment/benefit; goods, comfort

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

3.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
3.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
3.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

4.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
4.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

5.meaning: 'To us / toward us' — the preposition 'to/toward' joined to the pronoun 'us,' expressing direction or motion toward the speakers.
5.grammar: Preposition 'ilā' (to/toward), which shifts to the form 'ilay-' before a pronoun, plus the attached pronoun -nā, 'us.' Pronouns after a preposition stand in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -nā is a fixed form and does not change shape.
5.root: — (preposition + pronoun)

6.meaning: Their place or act of return — the destination to which a group comes back, their returning or homecoming.
6.grammar: A noun of place/occasion built on the ma- pattern ('the place or moment of returning'), with the attached pronoun -hum ('their,' a male/mixed group) showing possession. The -u ending on the noun is the nominative case, typically marking the subject or the thing being identified ('their return [is …]').

7.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
7.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

8.meaning: We cause them to taste — to make someone experience or undergo something, letting them feel its effect firsthand. The 'tasting' is a vivid metaphor for being made to sense a consequence directly.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb in form IV with an attached object pronoun. The nu- prefix means 'we' (the doer), and the suffix -hum(u) means 'them' (the ones affected); the -u on the verb-stem is the indicative, stating a plain fact, and the vowel on -humu is a connecting helper before the next word.

9.meaning: The punishment, chastisement, or torment — a penalty inflicted as retribution, especially the painful suffering of divine reckoning.
9.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the punishment'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb or the subject/predicate after certain particles.
9.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment; the inflicting of pain

10.meaning: The severe, intense, or harsh — that which is strong, hard, and forceful in degree. As an adjective it intensifies whatever it describes, marking it as grave and unsparing.
10.grammar: A singular masculine adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl, carrying the definite article (assimilated to sh-shadīd). The final -a ending marks the accusative case, commonly used for the object of a verb or a noun being described in that role.
10.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, severe

11.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
11.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
11.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

12.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
12.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

13.meaning: A present/ongoing verb meaning 'they disbelieve / they reject faith' — they cover over and deny the truth, refusing to acknowledge it. The underlying root sense is to cover or conceal, hence to be ungrateful and to deny.

parts.en: verbal stem: disbelieve / reject / be ungrateful

13.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject doing the action now or habitually — 'they disbelieve.' The full -ūna ending (rather than shortened -ū) signals the indicative mood, used for plain statements of fact.
13.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover/conceal; hence disbelief and ingratitude

1.meaning: 'And recite / and read aloud / and follow closely'. A command to recite or read out something, with an underlying sense of following it along, word by word. The front particle adds 'and'.
1.grammar: An imperative (command) to one male: 'recite'. The final long -u is the natural ending of this command from a verb whose root ends in a weak letter. Prefixed wa- means 'and'.
1.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read out, follow

2.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
2.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
2.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: 'News / tidings / a momentous report'. The word naba' means an announcement of weight and significance — not idle talk but news of consequence.
3.grammar: A noun in the accusative case. The stem ends in the hamza (the third radical of the root), and the case is shown only by the fatḥa (-a) borne on that hamza. The accusative is the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb (the thing being recited, told, or given).

4.meaning: Noah — the proper name of the Prophet Nūḥ.
4.grammar: A proper name. The -in ending (nunation) shows it is treated as a fully declinable noun in the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or to link to a preceding word. (Most personal names are partly indeclinable, but this short name takes full case endings.)

5.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
5.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

6.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
6.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

7.meaning: 'To/for his people' — a compound joining the preposition 'to/for', the noun 'people' (a community or folk, especially one's own kinfolk and nation), and 'his'. It expresses a community belonging to, or addressed by, a single male individual.
7.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') governs the noun, which therefore takes the genitive -i ending — the case that regularly follows a preposition or links one noun to another ('… of …'). The attached -hi means 'his'; the i-vowel form -hi (rather than -hu) is used because it harmonises with the preceding -i sound.
7.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

8.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
8.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
8.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

9.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
9.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

10.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

10.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

11.meaning: A finite past-tense verb meaning 'it became great/weighty/burdensome' — that something grew large, heavy, hard to bear, or oppressive to the heart. Often used of a matter felt as overwhelming or intolerably difficult.
11.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The intransitive vowel pattern (-u- in the middle) indicates an inherent quality — it 'is/became' great rather than acting on something. The final -a is the standard ending of this past-tense form.
11.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, magnitude, being big/weighty

12.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
12.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

13.meaning: My standing-place or station — the position where one stands, one's residence, post, or continued presence in a place. With the attached 'my', it denotes one's own standing or staying.
13.grammar: A masculine noun of place (the ma- pattern denotes a place or time of an action) with the possessive suffix -ī ('my'). When 'my' is attached, it takes the place of the usual case-vowel, so the ending here marks possession ('my standing') rather than a particular case.
13.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise, to establish

14.meaning: And my reminding or admonition — the act of calling something to mind, exhorting and recalling people to what they should heed. With 'my' attached, it denotes one's own reminding.
14.grammar: A verbal noun of form II (which carries the sense of 'causing to remember') with the prefix wa- ('and') and the possessive suffix -ī ('my'). The attached 'my' takes the place of the case-vowel, so the ending marks possession ('my reminding').
14.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention, to remind

15.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
15.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
15.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

16.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
16.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

17.meaning: Then upon / so upon — a linking word joining what follows to what came before ('then', 'so'), combined with the preposition 'upon/on/over', which indicates resting on, obligation, or being against something.
17.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('then, so', showing sequence or consequence) joined to the preposition ʿalā ('upon, over'). As a particle, ʿalā has a fixed form and does not change its ending; it puts the noun that follows into the genitive and conveys 'on, upon, against, or incumbent upon'.

18.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
18.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

19.meaning: I placed my trust, I relied wholly — to commit one's affairs entirely to another and depend on Him, resting in reliance. The verb's intensive pattern conveys deliberate, complete entrusting.
19.grammar: A past-tense verb in a reflexive intensive pattern (carrying the sense of taking something fully upon oneself — 'to entrust oneself, rely'). The -tu ending means the doer is 'I' and the action is completed.
19.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, appoint as guardian, rely upon

20.meaning: So resolve firmly / agree together — a command to make up your minds decisively and unite upon a course of action, gathering your resolve and settling your purpose with one accord.
20.grammar: A command (imperative) verb of form IV, prefixed with fa- ('so, then'). The -ū ending marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all'), directing the order to a group; the alif of fa-ajmiʿū is the imperative-forming prefix.

21.meaning: Your affair, matter, or plan — a concern, command, or course of action, here marked as belonging to a group ('your'). It spans a 'matter/business' on one hand and a 'command/decision' on the other.
21.grammar: A masculine noun with the attached possessive -kum ('your', addressing several people). The -a before the suffix marks the accusative case, which commonly marks the object of a verb ('your affair' as the thing acted upon).
21.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command, order; affair, matter

22.meaning: And your associate-partners — those whom people set up alongside Allah, or join to themselves as helpers, allies, or fellow decision-makers. The base noun denotes ones taken as partners or sharers, often with the sense of the false 'partners' wrongly associated with Allah.
22.grammar: A plural noun carrying the prefixed 'wa' ('and') and the attached pronoun '-kum' ('your', addressing a group). The '-a' ending is accusative, the form a noun typically takes when it is the object of a verb or otherwise governed as a direct complement.
22.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — sharing, partnership, associating others (with Allah)

23.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
23.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

24.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
24.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

25.meaning: A present-tense form of the verb 'to be / to exist / to happen', in a shortened (jussive) shape often carrying the sense 'it is' or, with a negating particle, 'it is not / was not'.
25.grammar: The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The verb is in the jussive mood, shown by the bare final consonant with sukūn (-n, no vowel) and the dropped long vowel of the root; this clipped form appears after certain particles (such as those that negate or command) and signals it is governed by one of them rather than standing as a plain statement.
25.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

26.meaning: Your affair, matter, command, or course of action — the thing one decides upon, orders, or sets out to do. The base noun 'amr' spans both a 'command/order' and a 'matter/concern' that is being managed or resolved.
26.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('your', addressing a group). The '-u' ending is nominative, the form a noun typically takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being described ('your affair is …').
26.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — commanding, ordering; an affair or matter

27.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
27.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

28.meaning: Grief, anguish, or oppressive distress — a weight of sorrow that covers and suffocates the heart. The word names a smothering gloom of the spirit; by extension, since the root means 'covering', it can also describe a matter left murky or unclear rather than openly settled, but its dominant sense is grievous distress.
28.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn) marks it as accusative and indefinite ('a/some …'), the form a noun typically takes as the object of a verb or as a predicate after certain particles.
28.root: غ-م-م (gh-m-m) — covering, overshadowing; gloom, grief, distress

29.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
29.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

30.meaning: Carry it out! Decree, decide, conclude, or settle the matter — a command to bring something to its final resolution. The verb 'qaḍā' means to determine and complete a thing decisively.
30.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group. The opening 'i-' is the helping vowel that begins many command forms, and the '-ū' ending directs the order to several people ('you all, carry it out!').

31.meaning: 'To me / toward me.' It joins the preposition ilā, meaning 'to / toward,' with an attached first-person 'me,' expressing motion or direction toward the speaker.
31.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to / toward' with the attached pronoun 'me.' The base preposition is ilā, ending in a long vowel (written with alif maqsūra, ى). When the 'me' pronoun attaches, that final long vowel turns into yāʾ and merges with the pronoun's yāʾ, giving a doubled, stressed -ayya — the whole word reading ilayya, 'to me.'

32.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
32.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

33.meaning: A negated or conditional verb meaning 'you (all) grant respite / give a delay.' From a root for looking and waiting, it means to give someone time, hold off, or postpone action against them.
33.grammar: Present-tense verb for a plural 'you,' shown by the tu- prefix ('you') and the -ū ending (masculine plural). The verb is in a subjunctive/jussive mood (after a negating or conditioning particle), which drops the mood-marking nūn (nūn al-iʿrāb) of the plural; the nūn that then appears, -ni, is the nūn al-wiqāya (protective nūn) that precedes a first-person object, whose pronoun yāʾ is elided but understood as 'me.' The causative form (Form IV) gives the sense 'cause to wait, grant a delay.'
33.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, wait, observe; (Form IV) to grant respite

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
1.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

2.meaning: "You turned away / turned your backs / took charge" — the verb means to turn away, turn aside, or turn one's back; in another sense to take charge of or befriend. The form carries a 'you' (plural) subject.
2.grammar: A past-tense reflexive/intensive verb with the attached subject suffix '-tum' ('you all'), marking a completed action done by the plural addressees. The '-tum' ending is what makes the verb mean 'you (all) did it'.
2.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near / turn toward or away / take charge

3.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
3.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

4.meaning: I asked you — a past-tense act of requesting, demanding, or seeking something from a group of people, whether a question posed or a favour sought.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb. The '-tu' ending means the speaker did it ('I asked'), and the attached '-kum' is the object ('… you', a group). Together they frame a completed request made by one person to many.

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — payment earned in return for work, effort, or service, whether earthly compensation or divine reward.
6.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn) marks it as genitive and indefinite, the form a noun typically takes after a preposition, or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of a reward').
6.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for effort

7.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
7.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

8.meaning: My reward, my wage, my recompense — the payment or return that is due specifically to the speaker for what they have done.
8.grammar: A singular noun with the attached pronoun '-iya' ('my'). When the possessive '-ī/-iya' is joined, it stands in place of the usual case-vowel, so the noun reads simply as 'my reward', the thing belonging to the speaker.
8.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for effort

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
9.root: — (particle)

10.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
10.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
10.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: And I have been commanded — a past-tense statement in which the speaker reports being ordered or instructed by another; the doer of the commanding is left unnamed, so the focus rests on the speaker as the one under orders.
12.grammar: A past-tense passive verb with the prefixed 'wa' ('and'). The inner vowel pattern 'u-i' shows it is passive ('was commanded', no named commander), and the '-tu' ending makes the speaker its subject ('I was commanded').
12.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — commanding, ordering; an affair or matter

13.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
13.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

14.meaning: '(that) I be / I should be' — the verb 'to be/become' in the first person, used in a dependent sense ('that I be…', 'lest I be…'). It expresses entering into or belonging to a described state.

parts.en: be / become (stem, ending in the subjunctive vowel -a)

14.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to be/become' with the 'I' prefix (a-). The stem ends in the third root letter ن, which carries the final short vowel -a; this -a is the subjunctive ending, the form used after particles such as 'that', 'so that', or 'lest' — so it reads 'that I be / I should be' rather than the plain statement 'I am' (which would end in -u).
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to become, to come into existence

15.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
15.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

16.meaning: The ones who submit/surrender — those who give themselves wholly to Allah in willing obedience and peace (the Muslims). As an active participle it names people characterized by this submission.
16.grammar: The prefix al- is 'the'. The stem is the Form IV active participle 'one who submits/surrenders'. The ending -īna is the sound masculine plural in the genitive/accusative state (the form used after prepositions, as object, or when linked to a preceding noun); its nominative counterpart would be -ūna. So: 'the ones who submit'.

1.meaning: So they denied him / cried lies against him — a group rejected a single masculine figure as a liar, with a connector ('so/then') showing it follows as a consequence.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb for a masculine plural subject ('they', shown by the -ū ending) in an intensive pattern meaning to actively charge someone with lying. It is opened by fa- ('so/then'), which links it as a result of what preceded. The attached -hu is the object 'him'.
1.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — lying, falsehood, denying as untrue

2.meaning: So We rescued him — a past-tense act of delivering and saving someone, bringing a person safely out of danger or destruction. The doubled-letter form intensifies it into a thorough, decisive rescue.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb of the intensive (doubled-middle) pattern, prefixed with 'fa' ('so/then'). The '-nā' ending means 'we' did it, and the attached '-hu' is the object ('… him'), giving 'so We delivered him'.
2.root: ن-ج-و (n-j-w) — deliverance, rescue, escaping to safety

3.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
3.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

4.meaning: (Who are) with him — the preposition 'with' (denoting accompaniment or being in someone's company) joined to the pronoun 'him'.
4.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment ('with') with the attached pronoun -hu ('him'). The pronoun is in the form used after a word ending in -a; together the phrase means 'with him / alongside him'.

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
5.root: — (particle)

6.meaning: The ship, ark, or vessel — a craft that floats and travels upon water; the word serves as both singular ('ship') and collective ('ships').
6.grammar: A definite noun (the al- prefix means 'the') with the -i (genitive) ending, the case that typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of the ship'). The form can denote one ship or ships collectively.
6.root: ف-ل-ك (f-l-k) — ships; also the circling orbit/sphere

7.meaning: And We made them / appointed them / turned them into — a past-tense act of bringing about, designating, or rendering a group into a certain state or role. 'Jaʿala' covers both creating/placing and assigning a quality.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb with the prefixed 'wa' ('and'). The '-nā' ending means 'we' did it, and the attached '-hum' is the object ('… them'), giving 'and We made them'.
7.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — making, placing, appointing, rendering into

8.meaning: Successors, deputies, inheritors — those who come after others and take their place, holding a position handed on to them (as stewards or vice-gerents on the earth). It is the plural of 'khalīfah'.
8.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural on the pattern 'khalāʾif', plural of 'khalīfah' ('successor, deputy'). The final -a is the accusative case, here typically the direct object or the role assigned ('made you successors'). Such 'diptote' plurals take -a rather than -an even when indefinite. It denotes those who succeed and take others' place.
8.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, succeed, leave behind

9.meaning: "and We drowned (something/someone)" — a past-tense verb of causing to sink and perish in water; the "We" is the majestic/plural divine subject.
9.grammar: Form-IV causative past-tense verb ("to make sink, to drown"). The attached -nā ending is the subject "we," marking a completed action done by a plural/majestic doer; the leading wa- is the connective "and."
9.root: غ-ر-ق (gh-r-q) — to sink, be submerged, drown

10.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
10.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

11.meaning: They denied / they cried lies; they declared (something or someone) to be false. An intensive verb meaning to reject as a lie, to disbelieve and brand untrue — directed by a plural 'they'.

parts.tr: kadhdhab (doubled dh; simplified transliterations may write 'kadhab')
parts.en: denied / branded as lies (past stem, intensive)

11.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in an intensive pattern (to treat as false, to repeatedly deny). The middle radical carries a shadda (doubling), which is exactly what marks this as the intensive form: kadhdhab- (not the simple kadhab-). The ending -ū marks the doers as 'they' — a plural, grammatically masculine group, so the whole reconstructs to kadhdhabū. Note that simplified transliterations sometimes omit the doubling and write 'kadhabū', but the doubled dh is essential to the form. The perfect tense denotes a completed action.
11.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this form, to call a lie, to deny as false

12.meaning: By/in Our signs. Āyāt is the plural of āya — a sign, token, or evidence. Signs are pointers that indicate a greater reality. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'with/in Our signs'.
12.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, in, by'), which requires the following noun to take the -i (genitive) ending. The attached -nā means 'our' when joined to a noun. The genitive here is governed by the preposition.

13.meaning: So look! / then observe! — a command to one person to look at, consider, and reflect upon something.
13.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'you', prefixed by fa- ('so/then'), which links it as a consequence of what precedes. The verb urges one to look and reflect: 'so look!' / 'then consider!'
13.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, see, observe, consider

14.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
14.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

15.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

15.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
15.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

16.meaning: The outcome, end-result, or final consequence — what a matter or a course of conduct ultimately comes to. It names the end that follows from a beginning.
16.grammar: A feminine noun. The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or, without nunation as here, the first term of a possessive phrase ('the outcome of …'). It denotes that which comes at the heel — the consequence that follows on.
16.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow, come after (at the heel); an end, consequence

17.meaning: Those who were warned — people to whom a warning of consequence or danger has been delivered. The form names the recipients of an admonition, the ones cautioned by a warner.
17.grammar: A passive participle ('one who has been warned') with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive state — the form used for such a plural noun when it is an object or follows a preposition or a linking noun.
17.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — warning, cautioning, giving notice of danger

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

2.meaning: We sent/raised up — to dispatch or commission someone (especially to send a messenger); the root also carries the sense of stirring up or raising to life.
2.grammar: Past-tense verb. The attached -nā ending means 'we' and marks a completed past action ('we sent'). The ending is the subject-marker for a first-person plural that has acted.
2.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to send forth, dispatch, raise up, resurrect

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: 'After him / it' — 'baʿd' denotes what comes afterward in time or sequence, here joined to 'him/it'.
4.grammar: A time-noun 'baʿd' (afterness) with an attached pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. The '-i' vowel on 'baʿd' is its case ending, set by 'baʿd's' own position in the sentence (commonly governed by a preceding preposition), not by the suffix; the attached '-hi' is the possessor ('him/it'), and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive. The pronoun's 'i'-vowel (-hi rather than -hu) follows because it comes after a genitive '-i'.

5.meaning: 'messengers' — envoys, those sent by Allah bearing a message to people.
5.grammar: The broken (irregular) plural of rasūl ('messenger'). The -an ending is accusative with tanwīn, typically marking the word as a direct object and indefinite ('messengers').
5.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; messenger, message

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
6.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

7.meaning: Their people — the folk, nation, or community to which they belong; one's own kin and tribe. 'Qawm' denotes a body of people bound together as a group.
7.grammar: A singular collective noun with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' ending is genitive — the form a noun takes after a preposition, or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of their people').
7.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — standing, rising; a people who stand together

8.meaning: So they came to them — a past-tense act of a group arriving at or coming up to another group, whether approaching, reaching, or confronting them.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb prefixed with 'fa' ('so/then'). The '-ū' ending means 'they' (a group) did it, and the attached '-hum' is the object ('… them'), giving 'so they came to them'.

9.meaning: 'With the clear proofs / evident signs' — bayyināt are plain, self-evident demonstrations that make the truth manifest, leaving no doubt.
9.grammar: Built from 'bi-' ('with/by means of') + 'al-' ('the') + a feminine plural noun meaning 'clear proofs.' The -i ending is the genitive case, required after the preposition 'bi-'; the feminine sound plural '-āt' takes -i (not -a) in this case. The whole phrase means 'with the clear proofs.'
9.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — clarity, distinctness, making plain

10.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
10.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

11.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
11.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

12.meaning: A verb phrase meaning 'so that they would believe' or 'in order for them to believe'. The underlying act is having faith — accepting and trusting in a truth, especially faith in Allah and His message.
12.grammar: li- is the particle 'so that / in order that', which puts the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood (expressing purpose or intended result). The verb is the Form IV present yu'minu, 'to believe / have faith'. The plural ending normally -ūna loses its final -na to become -ū because of the subjunctive, and the doer is 'they' (a group of males).

13.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
13.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

14.meaning: They denied / they cried lies; they declared (something or someone) to be false. An intensive verb meaning to reject as a lie, to disbelieve and brand untrue — directed by a plural 'they'.

parts.tr: kadhdhab (doubled dh; simplified transliterations may write 'kadhab')
parts.en: denied / branded as lies (past stem, intensive)

14.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in an intensive pattern (to treat as false, to repeatedly deny). The middle radical carries a shadda (doubling), which is exactly what marks this as the intensive form: kadhdhab- (not the simple kadhab-). The ending -ū marks the doers as 'they' — a plural, grammatically masculine group, so the whole reconstructs to kadhdhabū. Note that simplified transliterations sometimes omit the doubling and write 'kadhabū', but the doubled dh is essential to the form. The perfect tense denotes a completed action.
14.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this form, to call a lie, to deny as false

15.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
15.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

16.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
16.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

17.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
17.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
17.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

18.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
18.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
18.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

19.meaning: We seal / We set a stamp upon — a present-tense act of closing something off so nothing enters or leaves, as a seal closes a letter. Used of hearts, it pictures them shut against guidance or truth.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'na-' prefix means 'we' are the doers, and the '-u' on the end is the ordinary present-tense ending a verb carries when it stands as a plain statement ('we seal').

20.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
20.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

21.meaning: Hearts — the inner organ understood as the seat of feeling, intention, understanding, and faith. 'Qulūb' is the plural of 'qalb' (heart).
21.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') with the -i ending, the genitive case — which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the hearts') or follows a preposition ('in the hearts').
21.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over; the heart, that which fluctuates and turns

22.meaning: The transgressors / those who overstep limits / aggressors — people who habitually exceed the bounds of what is right and commit aggression.
22.grammar: An active participle (one who does the action) in the eighth pattern, masculine plural, carrying the definite article al- ('the'). The -īna ending is the masculine-plural ending used for the accusative or genitive case — typically the object of a verb or following a preposition.
22.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — to overstep, exceed; enmity, aggression

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

2.meaning: We sent/raised up — to dispatch or commission someone (especially to send a messenger); the root also carries the sense of stirring up or raising to life.
2.grammar: Past-tense verb. The attached -nā ending means 'we' and marks a completed past action ('we sent'). The ending is the subject-marker for a first-person plural that has acted.
2.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to send forth, dispatch, raise up, resurrect

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: "after them / following them" — the noun baʿd ('after, afterward') with the attached pronoun 'them', denoting what comes later in time than a group.
4.grammar: A time-noun used like a preposition, with an attached pronoun. The -i ending is genitive, the form taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive link. The suffix -him means 'them' (its vowel is -hi- to harmonise with the preceding -i).

5.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet sent to Pharaoh and the Children of Israel.
5.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. It is indeclinable — its ending does not change to show case (subject, object, or possessive); the long final -ā stays fixed whatever its role in a sentence.

6.meaning: A linking phrase 'and Aaron' — joining the proper name of the Prophet Hārūn with 'and'.
6.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus a proper name. It ends in -a and is a 'diptote' — a noun that does not take full case endings, so it shows -a (not -un/-in) and no nunation; this -a form covers both the object and after-a-preposition roles.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
7.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

8.meaning: Pharaoh — the title/name of the ruler of ancient Egypt, used as a proper name for that figure.
8.grammar: A proper name. Being a foreign, non-inflecting (diptote) name, it takes a single -a for both the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn. Here it follows another noun in a possessive link ('… of Pharaoh').

9.meaning: And his chiefs / his notables — the leading men, counsellors, and prominent figures around a ruler. 'Mala'' denotes the eminent assembly whose opinion fills the eye and carries weight.
9.grammar: A collective noun with the prefixed 'wa' ('and') and the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive — the form a noun takes after a preposition, or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of his chiefs').
9.root: م-ل-ء (m-l-ʾ) — filling; an assembly of eminent men who fill the eye

10.meaning: By/in Our signs. Āyāt is the plural of āya — a sign, token, or evidence. Signs are pointers that indicate a greater reality. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'with/in Our signs'.
10.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, in, by'), which requires the following noun to take the -i (genitive) ending. The attached -nā means 'our' when joined to a noun. The genitive here is governed by the preposition.

11.meaning: So they grew proud / were arrogant — to swell with self-importance, to be haughty and refuse out of pride to submit or accept the truth.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb in the form X pattern (istakbara, 'to be arrogant'), 3rd person masculine plural ('they'). The -ū ending shows a plural subject performing the completed action. The fa- prefix marks sequence or contrast ('so, but then').
11.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great; (form X) to deem oneself great, be arrogant

12.meaning: A compound meaning 'and they were' or 'and they used to' — it sets a state or habit in the past. The verb 'to be/become' here establishes an ongoing past condition, often paired with a following verb to express habitual action.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb ('to be') in the third-person masculine plural — the -ū ending means 'they' did/were. It commonly conveys a continued past state or habit, especially when followed by another verb. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

13.meaning: 'A people, a folk, a community' — a group of human beings bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared standing.
13.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action.
13.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group, people

14.meaning: Wrongdoers / criminals / guilty ones — those who commit grave sins and crimes, who deliberately cut themselves off from right and break with what is good.
14.grammar: An active participle of the form IV pattern (ajrama, 'to commit a crime'), sound masculine plural ('wrongdoers'). The -īna ending is the plural form used when the noun is an object or follows a preposition (the oblique/genitive-accusative case), as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
14.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to commit a crime, sin, cut off

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
1.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

2.meaning: It came to them / he came to them: a completed act of arriving or coming, with the recipients ('them') built into the word.

parts.en: final vowel of the past-tense base (he/it)

2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he/it … '), expressing a completed action. In this form the 'he/it' subject carries no added suffix — the -a is simply the final vowel resting on the last root letter of the base, not a person marker. The attached -hum(u) is the object pronoun 'them'; its vowel is lengthened to -humu to ease pronunciation before a following word.

3.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
3.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
3.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: From us / in our presence / with us — denoting nearness, possession, or origin from a particular side. 'ʿInd' marks something held at, coming from, or belonging to a party.
5.grammar: An adverb of place ('at the presence of') with the attached pronoun '-nā' ('us/our'). It is a frozen form fixed in the genitive, the '-i' state being the form such a word takes; the whole means 'with us' or 'from our side'.
5.root: عِنۡد (ʿind) — a frozen adverb of place ('at, near, in the presence of'); not derived from a verbal root

6.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

7.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
7.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

8.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
8.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

9.meaning: Surely magic — an emphatic assertion that something is sorcery: an act of illusion, enchantment, or deceptive power. The opening 'la-' adds a stress of certainty, 'it is indeed magic'.
9.grammar: An indefinite noun carrying the emphatic prefix 'la-' ('surely, indeed'). The '-un' ending (tanwīn) marks it as nominative and indefinite ('a …'), the form a noun takes when it is the subject or predicate of a statement.
9.root: س-ح-ر (s-ḥ-r) — magic, sorcery, enchantment, illusion

10.meaning: Clear, plain, and self-evident; that which makes things manifest. The form carries an active sense: not merely 'clear in itself' but 'making clear,' something that openly displays its nature and leaves no ambiguity.
10.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word) on the form mufʿil, meaning 'one who/that which makes [something] clear.' The final -un is the indefinite nominative ending ('a …'), the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: Mūsā (Moses), the prophet — a proper name.
2.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. It is indeclinable — its ending (the long final 'ā') does not change to show case — so the same form serves whether it functions as subject, object, or after a preposition.

3.meaning: A question 'Do you (plural) say…?' — challenging or asking a group whether they assert or claim something, in the present tense.
3.grammar: An interrogative particle 'a-' ('do…?') prefixed to a present-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all') in the indicative (ongoing action); the leading 'a-' turns the statement into a question.

4.meaning: 'To/for the truth' — al-ḥaqq is that which is real, true, established, and rightfully due: reality as it actually is, the right that is owed, and truth as opposed to falsehood. With the prefix it means 'to the truth' or 'for the truth'.

parts.en: truth / reality / what is rightfully due

4.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') attached to the definite noun al-ḥaqq ('the truth'). The -i ending is genitive, the case regularly required after a preposition such as li-.
4.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, real, established, rightfully due

5.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the point that' something occurred — pointing to the moment a past event took place and often implying that one thing happened upon the completion of another. In other uses it can carry the sense of 'not yet'.
5.grammar: A particle (a small connecting word), not a noun or verb, so it has no case or tense ending. It introduces a clause and links it in time to another event — most often 'when / as soon as' a past action happened.

6.meaning: "he/it came to you" — a past verb "came" with the pronoun "you" as the one reached, i.e. something arrived at or reached a group of people.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base third-person masculine singular form ("he/it came"), with no extra subject suffix. The verb "to come" is intransitive, so the attached -kum is not a direct object but an indirect (dative) pronoun — "to you" (masculine plural), equivalent to "came to you (all)."

7.meaning: Is this magic? — the noun 'magic/sorcery' opened by the questioning particle 'a-', posing the matter as a question: 'is it sorcery?'
7.grammar: An indefinite noun opened by the interrogative prefix 'a-' that turns a statement into a yes/no question. The '-un' ending (tanwīn) is nominative and indefinite ('a …'), the form a noun takes as the subject or predicate of the sentence.
7.root: س-ح-ر (s-ḥ-r) — magic, sorcery, enchantment, illusion

8.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
8.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

9.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
9.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'he succeeds / prospers / attains salvation' — to thrive and reach what is sought while escaping what is feared; ultimate well-being and triumph, including success in the Hereafter.
10.grammar: Present-tense verb (form IV), third-person masculine singular ('he succeeds'). The yu- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending for a plain present statement.
10.root: ف-ل-ح (f-l-ḥ) — to prosper, succeed, attain, be saved

11.meaning: The magicians / the sorcerers — those who practise magic, the workers of enchantment and illusion.
11.grammar: An active participle ('one who does magic') with the definite article 'al-' (its 'l' assimilated into the following 's'). The '-ūna' ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative — the form used for such a plural when it is the subject of a sentence.
11.root: س-ح-ر (s-ḥ-r) — magic, sorcery, enchantment, illusion

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: "have you come to us?" — the question-marker "?" plus the past-tense verb "you came/arrived," with "us" as the destination.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb fronted by the interrogative particle a- ("is it that…?"). The -ta ending marks a single male "you" as the doer of the completed action; the suffix -nā is the object "us."

3.meaning: So that you may turn us away / divert us — expressing purpose: in order to draw us aside and away from something we hold to. 'Lafata' means to twist or turn a thing from its direction.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb opened by 'li-' ('so that, in order to') and carrying the object '-nā' ('us'). The 'ta-' prefix addresses 'you', and after 'li-' the verb takes the '-a' (subjunctive) ending, the form used to express purpose or intention ('so that you may turn us').

4.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
4.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

5.meaning: 'We found / came upon / discovered' — to find something, either by encountering it or by determining it to be in a certain state.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb with the '-nā' ending meaning 'we'. So it means 'we found' or 'we came upon'. The '-nā' suffix attached to the past-tense stem marks the doers as a 'we' (first-person plural).
5.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to come upon, to discover

6.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
6.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

7.meaning: 'Our fathers / forefathers / ancestors.' The plural of 'father,' denoting forebears and the line of those who came before, with the attached 'our' marking them as one's own ancestry.
7.grammar: A plural noun ('fathers') with the attached possessive -nā ('our'). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the case typically used to mark the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or certain adverbial roles.
7.root: أ-ب-و (ʾ-b-w) — father, fatherhood

8.meaning: And you may be / become / come to have — a present-tense form addressing one person, expressing their being in or coming into some state. From 'kāna', the verb of being and becoming.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb of 'being' prefixed with 'wa' ('and') and addressing one person ('you', masculine singular). The '-a' ending is subjunctive — the form a verb takes after a purpose word — so it reads 'and that you may be/become'.
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, becoming, coming into existence

9.meaning: To the two of you / for the two of you — a preposition meaning 'to, for, belonging to' fused with the dual 'you two' pronoun, expressing benefit or direction toward two addressees.
9.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') joined to the second-person dual pronoun -kumā ('you two'). The -kumā suffix specifically addresses exactly two people; the whole expresses direction, benefit, or possession toward both.

10.meaning: Greatness, grandeur, supremacy — loftiness and pride of rank; the quality of standing above all others in majesty and dominion. It can name both true divine grandeur and the haughty self-exaltation of the proud.
10.grammar: An abstract noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The '-u' ending is nominative — the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being affirmed ('the grandeur is …').

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
11.root: — (particle)

12.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
12.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

13.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
13.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

14.meaning: 'We' — the standalone pronoun for a speaker including others (or a single speaker of majesty). It stands alone to name or emphasize the subject 'we'.
14.grammar: A detached (standalone) personal pronoun, first-person plural, 'we'. Such independent pronouns are used to state or emphasize the subject, often highlighting 'we' as the ones who do or are something.

15.meaning: To the two of you / for the two of you — a preposition meaning 'to, for, belonging to' fused with the dual 'you two' pronoun, expressing benefit or direction toward two addressees.
15.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') joined to the second-person dual pronoun -kumā ('you two'). The -kumā suffix specifically addresses exactly two people; the whole expresses direction, benefit, or possession toward both.

16.meaning: A noun meaning 'believers' — those who have faith, who trust and affirm as true. The underlying verbal idea is to grant security and trust, so a 'believer' is one who places trustful faith (and is also one who is granted security). The attached preposition 'bi-' gives the sense 'with / as believers.'
16.grammar: A Form IV active participle (one who has/causes faith and security), masculine plural. The plural ending appears as -īna rather than -ūna because it is the oblique (genitive/accusative) form, required here after the preposition 'bi-' ('with/as'). The whole word is therefore in the genitive.

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: Pharaoh; the title/name of the ruler of ancient Egypt, used as a proper name.
2.grammar: A proper noun (a foreign name, which does not take nunation). The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence (the one doing the action).

3.meaning: Bring to me! / Come to me with — a command to fetch, present, or bring something to the speaker. The verb 'atā' ('to come') in this form carries the sense of bringing a thing along.
3.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group, with the object '-nī' ('me'). The '-ū' ending directs the order to several people, and the attached '-nī' makes the speaker the one to whom they should bring ('you all, bring to me').
