11.meaning: 'So/then wait!' — a command addressed to a group to wait, watch, or expect (an outcome), prefaced by a connective 'so/then.'
11.grammar: The prefix 'fa-' links to what precedes with the sense 'so/then, therefore.' 'Intaẓirū' is a Form VIII imperative addressed to a masculine plural 'you all': the '-ū' ending is the command form telling a group to do the action — here 'wait / expect / watch for.'
11.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, watch, await

12.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
12.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

13.meaning: An expression meaning 'with you' — combining the word for accompaniment, togetherness, or presence-alongside with the attached pronoun 'you' (a group). It signals being in the company of, or on the side of, the addressed people.
13.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment (maʿa, 'with/in the company of') carrying the attached pronoun -kum ('you,' for a group of males). It expresses togetherness or being alongside the people addressed.

14.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
14.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

15.meaning: 'The ones who wait / those who are watching and expecting' — the active participle 'one who waits/awaits' in the plural, made definite by 'the.'
15.grammar: 'Al-' is the definite article 'the.' 'Muntaẓir' is the Form VIII active participle, 'one who waits/expects.' The ending '-īna' is the sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive form (the case used for objects and after prepositions), so it means 'the ones who wait/expect.'
15.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, watch, await

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

2.meaning: We rescue, save, or deliver someone — bringing them safely out of danger, distress, or destruction. The doubled middle consonant (Form II) gives an intensive or causative force: to cause to escape, to set free from peril.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the intensive Form II pattern (formed by doubling the middle root letter). The nu- prefix marks a 'we' subject. The verb is built on a root whose last letter is weak, so it ends in a long -ī rather than a hard consonant.
2.root: ن-ج-و (n-j-w) — to be safe, escape; (Form II) to rescue, deliver

3.meaning: Our messengers — those sent to carry and deliver a message. The base noun refers to an envoy or apostle commissioned by another to convey words or a charge, and the attached possessive marks them as belonging to a 'we'/'us'.
3.grammar: Plural noun with the attached pronoun -nā ('our'). The -a ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case used for the direct object of a verb ('… our messengers' as the thing acted upon) or after certain particles; the suffix -nā marks first-person plural possession.
3.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send, dispatch a message

4.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
4.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
5.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
5.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

6.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
6.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
6.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

7.meaning: A right, a due, or an obligation — that which is true, real, and rightfully owed; an established duty. As an adverbial accusative it conveys "as a duty/obligation, in truth, bindingly."
7.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The '-an' (nunation on the fatḥa, with a following alif) often functions adverbially here — "as a binding duty" or "in truth" — describing the manner or affirming the statement.
7.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, right, established; truth, right

8.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
8.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

9.meaning: We save, rescue, or deliver — the same core sense of bringing to safety, here in the related Form IV pattern (to cause to escape). The shortened ending reflects a grammatical clipping rather than a change of meaning.
9.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the causative Form IV pattern with a 'we' subject (nu-). Its root ends in a weak letter; the final long vowel has been dropped (a 'jussive/shortened' form), which typically happens after certain particles or in commands and conditional clauses.
9.root: ن-ج-و (n-j-w) — to be safe, escape; (Form IV) to rescue, deliver

10.meaning: The believers — those who have faith. The active participle of a Form IV verb meaning 'to believe, to have faith, to grant security.' A muʾmin is one who affirms and trusts, and who thereby finds and gives security; the plural denotes the community of the faithful.
10.grammar: A definite masculine plural noun (active participle). The al- means 'the.' The plural ending -īna marks 'the believers' in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) case — the form used when the word is a direct object or follows a preposition.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
2.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

3.meaning: 'The people / mankind' — human beings collectively, people in general, humanity.
3.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article al- ('the'); the article's 'l' assimilates into the following 'n' (al-nās → an-nās). The -u ending marks the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the basic naming form of a noun.
3.root: ن-و-س / أ-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people, sociability

4.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
4.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
5.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

7.meaning: 'Doubt / uncertainty.' A noun for the wavering state of mind in which one is unsure and cannot settle on what is true — the opposite of firm certainty.
7.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('a doubt / some doubt'). The genitive -i is the form taken after a preposition — typically conveying 'in doubt' or 'of doubt.'
7.root: ش-ك-ك (sh-k-k) — to doubt, be uncertain, waver

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

9.meaning: My religion / my way of life — dīn denotes a complete system of belief, obedience, worship, and accountability to Allah; it also carries the senses of judgement and recompense. The attached -ī makes it 'my (dīn).'

parts.en: religion / way of obedience and recompense

9.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -ī, 'my.' The case ending is masked because the noun is joined to this 'my' suffix.
9.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, obedience, accountability, recompense

10.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
10.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

11.meaning: I worship / I serve in devotion — to direct worship, obedience, and humble submission toward someone. The root carries the idea of being a devoted servant.
11.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The a- prefix marks a first-person-singular subject ('I'). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain statement of fact ('I worship / I do worship').
11.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, submit as a devoted servant

12.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
12.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

13.meaning: You worship (Him) — to serve, devote oneself to, and submit in obedient adoration to a deity. The verb conveys total devotion: not merely outward ritual but the humble servitude a worshipper owes to the One worshipped.
13.grammar: Present/future-tense verb addressed to a group of males ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks second person ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural subjects and the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact, 'you do/will worship'), as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form which would drop the final -na.
13.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, submit as a devoted servant

14.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
14.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

15.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
15.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
15.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

16.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
16.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

17.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
17.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

18.meaning: I worship / I serve in devotion — to direct worship, obedience, and humble submission toward someone. The root carries the idea of being a devoted servant.
18.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The a- prefix marks a first-person-singular subject ('I'). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain statement of fact ('I worship / I do worship').
18.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, submit as a devoted servant

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
19.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

20.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
20.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

21.meaning: 'He takes you fully (in death/sleep) / receives you back in full' — the verb means to take something completely and in full, used especially of taking the soul at death (and, by extension, in sleep). With 'you all' as the object: He takes you wholly back.
21.grammar: A Form V present-tense verb with the 'ya-' prefix for 'he', and the object pronoun '-kum' ('you all', masculine plural). The verb ends in a weak long vowel '-ā' (the final root letter being a weak letter). The Form V pattern adds the sense of taking the thing completely and to oneself.
21.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — fulfilling, completing, taking in full

22.meaning: And I have been commanded — a past-tense statement in which the speaker reports being ordered or instructed by another; the doer of the commanding is left unnamed, so the focus rests on the speaker as the one under orders.
22.grammar: A past-tense passive verb with the prefixed 'wa' ('and'). The inner vowel pattern 'u-i' shows it is passive ('was commanded', no named commander), and the '-tu' ending makes the speaker its subject ('I was commanded').
22.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — commanding, ordering; an affair or matter

23.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
23.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

24.meaning: '(that) I be / I should be' — the verb 'to be/become' in the first person, used in a dependent sense ('that I be…', 'lest I be…'). It expresses entering into or belonging to a described state.

parts.en: be / become (stem, ending in the subjunctive vowel -a)

24.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to be/become' with the 'I' prefix (a-). The stem ends in the third root letter ن, which carries the final short vowel -a; this -a is the subjunctive ending, the form used after particles such as 'that', 'so that', or 'lest' — so it reads 'that I be / I should be' rather than the plain statement 'I am' (which would end in -u).
24.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to become, to come into existence

25.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
25.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

26.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
26.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

1.meaning: A two-part connector: 'and that.' The 'wa' joins what precedes, and 'an' is the subordinating particle 'that,' which introduces a following verb-clause (often steering it into the subjunctive) — used to report or quote a command, statement, or purpose.
1.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus the particle an, a subordinator meaning 'that' which heads a clause and commonly puts a following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood (often expressing purpose, intention, or reported speech). It is a particle and does not itself take a case ending.

2.meaning: Set up, establish, make upright, or keep steadfastly — a command to direct something firmly and keep it standing straight. With matters of worship it conveys performing them properly and consistently.
2.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single person, 'set [it] up / keep [it] firm.' It belongs to the causative Form IV pattern. The clipped, vowel-less ending (-m) is characteristic of the singular command form built on a weak-middle root.
2.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; (Form IV) to set up, establish, maintain

3.meaning: Your face; the front of the head — and by extension one's countenance or direction. Addressed to a single male ('your'), and here the object of an action.
3.grammar: The noun 'face' (wajh) with the attached pronoun -ka ('your', for one male). The -a ending before the pronoun is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb ('turn … your face').
3.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, that which one faces

4.meaning: To / for the religion — the noun dīn (a complete system of belief, obedience, worship, and accountability to Allah) preceded by the preposition li- ('to/for'), expressing direction toward it or devotion for its sake.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the religion') governed by the preposition li- ('to/for'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which is required after a preposition. (The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following d, written as a doubled d.)

5.meaning: 'Upright in faith, naturally inclined to pure monotheism' — one who turns away from all false worship toward sincere devotion to the one Allah; a term for steadfast, primordial monotheistic faith.
5.grammar: A singular indefinite noun/adjective (an intensive 'faʿīl' pattern). The -an ending is accusative plus nunation: it marks indefiniteness ('a/an') and the accusative case, the form used for an object, a descriptive term, or a circumstantial state ('… as one upright in faith').
5.root: ح-ن-ف (ḥ-n-f) — to incline away (from error) toward pure monotheism

6.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

7.meaning: You must certainly be / never be — an emphatic form of the verb 'to be', stressing that one truly will (or, with a negative, truly must not) be in a certain state.
7.grammar: A present-tense form of the verb 'to be', addressed to 'you' (the prefix ta-). The heavy ending -anna (nūn of emphasis) gives a strong, insistent force — 'you most certainly are/must be' — and is the standard way Arabic stresses a command or warning attached to a verb.
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

8.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
8.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

9.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
9.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.
9.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate, partner

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: You call upon, invoke, pray to, or summon. The verb daʿā covers calling out to someone, appealing to them for help, and supplication.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a second-person-masculine-singular subject ('you'). Built on a root whose last letter is weak: in the plain indicative this verb ends in a long -ū (tadʿū), but here the weak letter has dropped away, leaving the bare short -u of the shortened (jussive) form — the shape this verb takes after certain particles or in conditional clauses.
2.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, supplicate

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
4.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
4.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

8.meaning: It benefits you / profits you — to bring advantage, gain, or usefulness to someone. The attached -ka makes the object 'you.'
8.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person-masculine-singular subject ('he/it'), and the attached object pronoun -ka ('you'). The stem-vowel -u before the suffix reflects the indicative mood, a plain statement ('it benefits you').
8.root: ن-ف-ع (n-f-ʿ) — to benefit, profit, be useful

9.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
9.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

10.meaning: It harms you / hurts you / damages you — to bring injury, loss, or detriment to someone. The doubled final consonant belongs to the root itself. The attached -ka makes the object 'you.'
10.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person-masculine-singular subject ('he/it'), and the attached object pronoun -ka ('you'). The verb's two identical final letters are merged (a doubled consonant), the natural form for this kind of root.
10.root: ض-ر-ر (ḍ-r-r) — to harm, hurt, damage, cause loss

11.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
11.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

12.meaning: You did / you did it / you acted — the basic verb faʿala means to do, make, or perform an act. The -ta ending pins the doer as 'you.'
12.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb. The suffix -ta marks the subject as second-person-masculine-singular, 'you did.' Past-tense verbs of this kind attach the doer as an ending rather than a prefix.
12.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — to do, make, act, perform

13.meaning: A two-part opener meaning roughly 'then/so, truly You …': a connecting 'then/so' joined to an emphatic particle that asserts what follows with certainty, plus an attached 'You.' The emphatic particle (inna) strongly affirms the statement, like saying 'indeed' or 'it is certainly the case that.'
13.grammar: A particle cluster, not a verb. fa- is a connector ('then, so, and thus'). inna is an emphatic/affirming particle that places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative; here that pronoun is the attached -ka ('you,' one male), the topic being emphasized. There is no tense or case ending of its own.

14.meaning: In that case / then — a response particle signaling that what follows is the consequence of a just-stated condition or supposition ('if so, then…').
14.grammar: A response/consequence particle, not a noun or verb. The -an ending is a fixed part of the word (written with a final alif), not a live grammatical case. It introduces the result side of a hypothetical ('then you would…').

15.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
15.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

16.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
16.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: 'He/it touches you', 'it afflicts / befalls you'. The verb means to make contact with, and by extension for something (often harm) to reach or strike a person. The 'you' here is a single male.

parts.en: he / it — present/ongoing action; the doubled y reflects assimilation of a preceding particle's final letter into this prefix

2.grammar: Present-tense verb in a jussive (clipped) form with attached object 'you'. The prefix is the masculine 'he/it' marker, written with a doubling (shadda) because the final consonant of an immediately preceding particle has assimilated into it. The bare consonant ending of the stem (with the doubled root letter spelled out as msas) is the shortened form used after conditional particles. The -ka means 'you', addressed to one male.
2.root: م-س-س (m-s-s) — to touch, make contact, befall

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: 'With harm', 'with affliction / hurt'. The phrase joins the preposition 'with / by means of' to a word for harm, injury, or distress. The word is in its indefinite form: 'some harm', 'any affliction'.
4.grammar: A preposition 'with' attached to the noun 'harm'. The -in ending is the indefinite genitive: the genitive case (required after a preposition) combined with the 'an/some' nunation that marks the noun as unspecified — 'with some harm'.

5.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
5.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

6.meaning: 'Remover', 'one who uncovers / lifts away / dispels'. The word names the agent who unveils or takes away something — for instance lifting away harm or revealing what was hidden.
6.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun: 'one who removes/uncovers'). The -a ending is accusative, the case that commonly marks a word as a direct object or otherwise governs it into this case. As a doer-noun it can take an object after it.
6.root: ك-ش-ف (k-sh-f) — to uncover, unveil, remove, lay bare

7.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
7.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

8.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
8.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

9.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
9.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

10.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
10.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

11.meaning: He intends / wills / wants for you — to purpose or desire something. The verb is in the causative Form IV pattern (marked by a prefixed hamza in the base form, أراد), giving the sense of setting one's will toward an aim. The attached -ka marks 'you' as the one for/at whom the intention is directed.
11.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the causative Form IV pattern. The yu- prefix marks a third-person-masculine-singular subject ('he'), with the attached object pronoun -ka ('you'). The stem's vowel-less ending (-rid before the suffix) is the shortened/jussive form, typical after conditional particles ('if He wills…').
11.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, desire; (Form IV) to want, will, intend

12.meaning: Good, better, that which is beneficial — goodness itself, and by comparison 'more good / better'; also wealth or any benefit regarded as good.
12.grammar: A noun/comparative ('good' or 'better') carrying a prefixed preposition. The prefix bi- means 'with'; the final -in is the indefinite genitive (nunation), showing no 'the' and the genitive case taken after a preposition.
12.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, that which is good or preferable

13.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
13.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

14.meaning: One who repels, averts, turns back, or wards off — an active doer of the act of pushing something away or sending it back. As an active participle it names the one performing this repelling.
14.grammar: An active participle (a noun-like word meaning 'the one who does X'), here 'one who repels.' Built on a doubled root, its two identical letters are merged. The final -a is an accusative ending, the form a noun takes as a grammatical object or after certain particles (such as 'there is no …').
14.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to turn back, repel, avert, send back

15.meaning: For / of His bounty — faḍl denotes grace, favour, abundant generosity, and bestowed goodness beyond what is owed. The li- means 'for/of,' and the attached -hi makes it 'His.'
15.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition li- ('for/to/of') with the attached possessive pronoun -hi ('His'). After the preposition the noun is in the genitive, shown by the -i vowel before the -hi suffix.
15.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — grace, favour, bounty, excess of generosity

16.meaning: He causes (it) to reach / strikes / lets befall — to make something arrive at or hit a target; to afflict or bestow upon. The verb covers both reaching someone with good and striking them with hardship.

parts.en: cause to reach / make befall (Form IV stem)

16.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the causative Form IV pattern. The yu- prefix marks a third-person-masculine-singular subject ('he'). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain statement ('he causes [it] to reach').
16.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, be right; (Form IV) to make reach, befall, afflict

17.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
17.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

18.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
18.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

19.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
19.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
19.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

20.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
20.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

21.meaning: 'His servants / His slaves / His worshippers' — ʿibād are those who serve and worship; with the attached pronoun it denotes the servants belonging to Him (Allah), i.e., humankind or His devotees.
21.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel is the genitive case, typically appearing after a preposition or in a possessive ('of') link; the pronoun names the one to whom the servants belong.

22.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
22.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

23.meaning: The Oft-Forgiving — al-Ghafūr is an intensive form built on the idea of forgiveness: One who forgives much and repeatedly, who veils and pardons sins abundantly. It is one of the names by which Allah is described.
23.grammar: A definite noun/adjective ('the …') in an intensive pattern that signals doing something abundantly ('much-forgiving'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the form a word takes as a subject or predicate ('is the …').
23.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, pardon, cover over and veil sins

24.meaning: A name/quality meaning 'the Most Merciful' or 'the Bestower of mercy' — the One whose mercy is deeply felt and continually shown to His creation.
24.grammar: The definite article l- ('the') with an intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality of mercy. The -u ending marks nominative case, typical of a subject or of a word describing/identifying the subject.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
2.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

3.meaning: 'The people / mankind' — human beings collectively, people in general, humanity.
3.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article al- ('the'); the article's 'l' assimilates into the following 'n' (al-nās → an-nās). The -u ending marks the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the basic naming form of a noun.
3.root: ن-و-س / أ-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people, sociability

4.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

5.meaning: 'he/it came to you' — the arrival of someone or something to a group of people addressed.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb ('came'), done by 'he/it'. The verb is intransitive, so the attached -kum ('you,' plural) is not a direct object but a recipient/directional pronoun marking the people the arrival is toward ('came to you'); it is voweled -kumu before a following word. So: 'he/it came to you (all).'
5.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, arrive

6.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
6.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
6.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
7.root: — (preposition)

8.meaning: 'Your Lord' (addressing a group). 'Rabb' is a rich term: the Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, possesses, provides for, and brings a thing to its proper completion — far more than a mere ruler.
8.grammar: A noun ('Lord') with an attached possessive pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. 'Rabb' carries a doubled (geminated) 'b' — the shaddah — at its core. The '-i' vowel on 'rabb' is its case ending, determined by 'Lord's' own role in the sentence (not by the suffix); the attached '-kum' is the possessor ('your'), addressing a plural 'you', and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive.

9.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then whoever'. It joins a clause to what precedes ('so', 'then') and introduces a conditional or general statement about any person who does something ('whoever, anyone who').
9.grammar: The prefix fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so/then', linking this to a prior statement. man is a conditional/relative word for persons ('whoever'); its base form is man, and the final vowel here is read -i simply to ease pronunciation before a following consonant cluster, not a case ending.

10.meaning: He became guided / found the right way / accepted guidance — the verb (Form VIII) means to take the right path, follow guidance, and be rightly directed; it implies responding to and embracing guidance.

parts.en: became guided / followed the right way

10.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb in the Form VIII pattern (which often carries a reflexive sense — accepting guidance for oneself), with a third-person-masculine-singular subject ('he'). Its weak final root letter appears as a long -ā ending, the usual past-tense shape for such roots.
10.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead aright, show the way

11.meaning: A compound particle 'so it is only …' or 'then indeed only.' It joins a consequence ('so/then') to an emphatic restriction ('only / nothing more than'), confining the statement to exactly what follows.
11.grammar: A cluster of particles: 'fa-' introduces a result ('so/then'), 'inna' gives emphasis ('truly'), and the attached 'mā' turns the emphasis into restriction, so the whole means 'so it is only/nothing but.' These are connective and emphatic words; they have no case ending of their own.

12.meaning: He is guided / follows the right way — the present-tense counterpart of the same Form VIII verb: to take guidance, be rightly directed, and follow the correct path.

parts.en: be guided / follow the right way (Form VIII stem)

12.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the Form VIII pattern (often reflexive — taking guidance for oneself). The ya- prefix marks a third-person-masculine-singular subject ('he'). The root's weak final letter surfaces as a long -ī, and this full ending reflects the ordinary indicative (a plain statement).
12.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead aright, show the way

13.meaning: For / to himself / for his own soul — nafs means the self, soul, or person (the inner self that is held to account). The li- means 'for/to,' and the attached -hi makes it 'his.'
13.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition li- ('for/to') with the attached possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). After the preposition the noun is in the genitive, shown by the -i vowel before the -hi suffix.
13.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, person, the inner being

14.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
14.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

15.meaning: He strayed, lost the way, or went off course — to wander from the right path, whether literally or figuratively (to err, be misguided, or deviate from truth and guidance).
15.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he went astray'. The bare past-tense form with the -a ending signals a single male (or thing) as the doer of a completed action.
15.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

16.meaning: A compound particle 'so it is only …' or 'then indeed only.' It joins a consequence ('so/then') to an emphatic restriction ('only / nothing more than'), confining the statement to exactly what follows.
16.grammar: A cluster of particles: 'fa-' introduces a result ('so/then'), 'inna' gives emphasis ('truly'), and the attached 'mā' turns the emphasis into restriction, so the whole means 'so it is only/nothing but.' These are connective and emphatic words; they have no case ending of their own.

17.meaning: He goes astray / strays / errs / is lost — to wander from the right path, lose one's way, or fall into error. The doubled final consonant belongs to the root.
17.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person-masculine-singular subject ('he'). The two identical final root letters are merged (a doubled consonant), and the -u vowel on it marks the indicative mood, a plain statement ('he strays').
17.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

18.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
18.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

19.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
19.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

20.meaning: I — the standalone pronoun used to declare or emphasize the speaker himself as the one in view.
20.grammar: A detached first-person singular pronoun ("I"). Being an independent pronoun, it has a fixed form with no case ending; it is used to state or stress who the subject is.

21.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
21.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

22.meaning: A guardian, trustee, or one put in charge to manage another's affairs; a disposer of matters, an agent responsible for and relied upon to handle things. The prefixed bi- often serves to reinforce a preceding negation ('not a guardian at all').
22.grammar: A noun in the pattern of an intensive agent ('one entrusted/relied upon'), preceded by the preposition bi- ('with/as'). The ending -in is genitive and indefinite (the 'n' is nunation, marking 'a/an'): the genitive case is required after the preposition bi-.
22.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — entrusting, relying upon

1.meaning: And follow / pursue / comply with — the verb (Form VIII) means to follow after, walk behind, obey, and adhere to. The leading wa is the connective 'and.'
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single person, 'follow!', in the Form VIII pattern (often reflexive — to follow for oneself), carrying the connective wa ('and'). The clipped, vowel-less ending is characteristic of the singular command.
1.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue, comply

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: 'It is revealed / is inspired' — the act of conveying something by inspiration or revelation, expressed passively (the thing is made known to someone by a higher source).
3.grammar: A present-tense passive verb (form IV) in the third-person masculine singular ('it is …'). The yu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks the passive voice — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The final weak vowel -ā (written on a yā') is the ending of this weak-final root in the present tense, here read as an ongoing/repeated passive ('is being revealed').
3.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to reveal, inspire, convey by suggestion

4.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
4.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

5.meaning: And be patient / endure steadfastly / persevere — sabr is the disciplined restraint of the self: bearing hardship calmly, holding firm, and not giving way to impatience or despair. The leading wa is the connective 'and.'
5.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single person, 'be patient!', carrying the connective wa ('and'). The clipped, vowel-less ending is the normal shape of the singular command form.
5.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — to be patient, endure, restrain oneself, persevere

6.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
6.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

7.meaning: '(That) he judges, decides, rules, or gives a verdict.' The root concerns delivering a binding judgment, settling a matter authoritatively, and the wisdom that underlies sound rule.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine 'he.' The final -a vowel is the subjunctive ending, which typically appears after particles meaning 'that' or 'so that,' giving the sense 'that he may judge.'
7.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, rule, decide with wisdom

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
9.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

10.meaning: 'Best / the best (of)' — superior to all others in goodness, excellence, or worth; the finest in its class.
10.grammar: khayr functions as a comparative/superlative noun ('better / best'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or predicate of a sentence and also opens a possessive phrase ('the best OF …').
10.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, that which is good or best

11.meaning: Those who judge, decide, and govern — the ones who pass binding verdicts and exercise authoritative rule. The active participle from the root for judging denotes a doer of the act, so 'ḥākim' is 'one who judges/rules/arbitrates'; in the definite plural it means 'the judges' or 'those who decide,' and when used of Allah it carries the sense of the supremely wise, just Arbiter whose judgment is final.

parts.en: one who judges / rules / arbitrates (active participle)

11.grammar: An active participle (the 'doer' form) made definite by the article 'al-' ('the') and pluralised by the masculine sound-plural suffix '-īna,' giving 'the ones who judge/rule.' The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the genitive or accusative state — the case used after a preposition, in an oath, when a word is possessed ('… OF the judges'), or when the word is a direct object. (The matching subject form would end in '-ūna.')
11.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, govern, and exercise wise authority
